subject: Loan Processing Exception during Reschedule - “Interest Only Period should be less than the contract term”
urgency: Medium – 3: There is an impact to your business, but your business continues to function
description: Updating a Loan Account fails with loan.LoanProcessingException 'Interest Only Period should be less than the contract term', thrown in LoanAccountTriggerHandler.beforeUpdateHandler line 457. Root cause: after a backdated reschedule, Interest Only Period and Contract Term both end up equal to 22, and validation requires IOP strictly less than Contract Term.
issue_summary: A backdated loan reschedule leaves Interest Only Period equal to Contract Term (both 22), which fails an Apex validation requiring IOP < Contract Term, blocking further updates to the loan record.
case_fix: No permanent fix yet; the 2 affected contracts were manually data-fixed. Q2 replicated the bug (occurs when a prior reschedule reversal marks the current bill non-primary, combined with a backdated reversal where transaction date and repayment start date differ by 2 months while reducing IOP and contract term by 1) and escalated to Engineering for a proper fix.
case_discussion: Q2 acknowledged and reduced urgency since only 2 loans were affected; Rohit reproduced the issue with a smaller data set and identified the triggering combination of reschedule reversal + backdated reversal; case escalated to Engineering; as of the latest update the fix is still described as complex and in progress.
current_status: Open (Waiting on Q2 internal), Sub-status Pending Product - Bug. Engineering still investigating a fix; interim manual data-fix applied to the 2 known affected contracts.

subject: £303,076.99 of Billed Amount lost following Partial Redemption

description: Loan 1147 is in significant arrears (300K+ delinquent interest). case_discussion: Q2 initially could not diagnose without period logs; asked customer to replicate in sandbox; Anshu replicated and provided exact repro steps; Q2 (Rohit) explained the behaviour is by design; customer/Q2 agreed this doesn't satisfy Folk2Folk's business requirement, so a product enhancement was requested instead of a bug fix.

subject: Interest Posting on FOLK2FOLK
description: Contract LAI-1251: monthly repayment schedule shows interest of 2,166.67, but the July bill was generated for 2,166.66. When the interest LPT was cleared, the interest posting wasn't satisfied; when the fee LPT was cleared, 0.01 was allocated to interest and the system created a duplicate interest-posting record instead of satisfying the original one, leaving the original untouched.
issue_summary: A one-cent rounding/reversal discrepancy appears in interest postings on backdated payment clearances, where the system reverses and re-posts an Interest Posting Transaction (IPT) with slightly different rounding instead of satisfying the original record.
case_fix: No code fix - Q2 explained this is a rare, non-replicable-in-sandbox behaviour tied to backdated payments (when a Loan Payment Transaction is cleared after being backdated relative to the IPT, the IPT reverses and reposts, re-rounding by up to 0.01). Since the system self-corrects (reverses and reapplies the IPT) it was not treated as a blocker.
case_discussion: Extensive multi-month thread (60+ comments, Aug 2022-Jan 2023): customer repeatedly asked for updates; several calls scheduled; customer provided production and UAT access/org IDs and replicated the scenario in UAT (contract with 'Actual Interest Only Payments' = true); Q2 traced it to backdated LPT clearance vs. IPT timing and rounding; Q2's product team classified it as expected, low-impact behaviour.
current_status: Closed (24/01/2023) as explained system behaviour; customer asked to monitor in production and open a new case if it recurs.

subject: Interest waiver issue on FOLK2FOLK LAI - 1091
description: Contract LAI-1091: a series of transactions on 19th/23rd September 2022 (rejected payments, a fee waiver, a partial interest payment/waiver, then a reschedule) resulted in previously-waived interest being re-added as posted interest in the contract history, with no corresponding visible transaction/record explaining it.
issue_summary: After a reschedule following several waived/partial payments, previously waived interest reappeared as posted interest with no visible transaction explaining the change.
case_fix: Root cause was user behaviour, not a bug: editing the same loan in two browser tabs at once causes the tab with stale data to overwrite recent saves when it is later saved, reverting field values (without affecting any underlying transactions). Fix was procedural - avoid multi-tab editing of the same loan and refresh tabs after saving.
case_discussion: Several calls scheduled between customer and Q2; Q2 (B Sahana) explained the multi-tab race condition after review and advised on the workaround.
current_status: Closed (17/10/2022) - explained as multi-tab editing behaviour, not a system defect.

subject: Investor Payout Reversal Job did not pick the Record
description: Loan contract LAI-800: a payment transaction (LPT-000005762, cleared 02/10/2022) was reversed on 07/10/2022, but the overnight Investor Payout Reversal batch did not reverse the related Investor Loan Transaction (ILT), even when run manually with the record ID.
issue_summary: The Investor Payout Reversal batch job silently failed to reverse an ILT tied to a reversed loan payment transaction, and running it manually by record ID did not fix it either.
case_fix: Root cause was a large volume of Loan Transaction Summary records (16,112) causing 'Too many DML rows: 10001' errors on the batch job; fix was to delete the excess summary records in batches of 5000 via script (after confirming summary-generation flags were off on products) and rerun the job. A separate related product bug (null-object error converting an Application with prepaid fees to a contract) was fixed via Loan managed-package patches 3.5054.161 and then 3.5054.171. Remaining historic affected data was corrected manually.
case_discussion: Long thread (Oct 2022-Jun 2023): Q2 asked for LMA access and repro steps; customer provided sandbox steps and org IDs; investigation uncovered the DML row-limit issue and a separate prepaid-fee conversion bug; Q2 shipped two package patches (JIRA PDRFF-1599) and gave a script to purge excess transaction summaries; customer confirmed the patch worked in production after manual correction of affected past data.
current_status: Closed (20/06/2023) after patch installation and manual data correction.

subject: FOLK2FOLK : Investor payout is more than amount received in LPT-000007134
urgency: Constant
description: Contract LAI-1311: LPT-000007134 (£2,312.50, cleared 27/10/2022, fully satisfied towards interest) resulted in an investor payout of £4,445.16 - almost double the amount received from the borrower. Customer asked how/why investor payout could exceed the amount collected, and whether a configuration was missing. This case absorbed cases 03507910 and 03508069 covering similar over/under investor payout issues across many contracts.
issue_summary: Investor payouts were inconsistently more or less than the related loan payment amount across many contracts, rooted in how Interest-Only (IO) accrual, IO sales, and backdated/rescheduled certificate-rate changes interact with the Investor Payout Job's timing.
case_fix: Multiple Symphonix Loan package patches were released and installed over the life of the case, fixing several distinct JIRA-tracked bugs: PDRFF-1464 (original merged issue), PDRFF-1851 (Paid to Investor flag enabled with no ILT created), PDRFF-2095/ND-6728 (Paid to Investor flag not set true when an LPT pays a Charge amount), and PDRFF-2129/ND-6727 (error shown when Investor Payout Job runs after an IO sale). Interim workaround was enabling Interest Posting on Investment Orders and including IO Accrual/IO Posting jobs in the start-of-day batch sequence. Loan package versions 3.5054.172 and later 3.5054.179 (plus supporting Utilities/FileGen/Common/Integration/Marketplace/Notify packages) were installed in production; customer confirmed the fix worked after installation and manual correction of historic affected data.
case_discussion: This was Q2's longest-running investor-payout investigation (Oct 2022-Oct 2023): many calls, extensive log analysis, and iterative patch releases; customer supplied long lists of affected LAI/LPT numbers each time a new patch surfaced further edge cases (backdated rescheduling, IO sales, early/late LPT clearance relative to due date); Q2 progressively raised and fixed several JIRAs as each new pattern was isolated.

subject: Billing job failed for LAI - 915 in production
description: Contract LAI-915 (due date 23rd monthly): the November billing job threw an exception and no bill or LPT was generated, even though pre-bill days (11) meant the bill should have been generated on 12/11/2022.
issue_summary: The monthly billing batch job failed outright for one contract, preventing that month's bill and payment transaction from being created.

Q2 manually corrected Actual_Next_Installment_Date to 23/11/2022 and reran the billing job, which generated the bill successfully; both date fields were left properly in sync to prevent recurrence.

current_status: Closed (30/11/2022) after the date field was corrected and the bill generated.

subject: February and march payment difference
urgency: Constant
description: With interest-only behaviour set to 'actual' in production, loans with due dates of 29/30/31 (e.g. LAI-1200) show a different repayment schedule specifically for the February and March periods compared to the rest of the year. Customer asked for a workaround.
issue_summary: Loans due on the 29th-31st show inconsistent Feb/March interest schedules under the 'actual' interest-only day-count method, and the customer wanted a workaround.
case_fix: No fix - Q2 confirmed this is expected behaviour of the 'months and days' time-counting method: a 30-day period is assumed for all months, so Feb is effectively a 29-day period and March a 31-day period relative to fixed due dates, which is normal and replicable in Q2's own org. Case was later reopened in Jan 2024 for a possible product enhancement, with Symphonix product team exploring options and planning a customer walkthrough (targeted Oct 2025).
case_discussion: Q2 replicated the same Feb/March pattern internally and explained the day-count method; case was closed as expected behaviour (Jan 2023), reopened a year later (Jan 2024) at the customer's request for a fresh look, and as of Sept 2025 Symphonix product team was still exploring potential product options to present to Folk2Folk.
current_status: Closed, but effectively an open follow-up track - most recent update (25/09/2025) has Q2 product team still working on potential options/enhancement, walkthrough planned for October.

subject: Invalid date/ time error in production
urgency: Intermittent
description: In production, reversing an LPT or running the investor payout job sometimes fails because certain LPT/Interest Posting snapshots contain an invalid date/time value (examples: LAI-1037, LAI-676, LAI-1193).
issue_summary: Some LPT and interest-posting snapshot records contain a malformed date/time value, causing LPT reversals and the investor payout job to fail intermittently.
case_fix: Root cause: Salesforce enforced a change to locale date/time formats, and the LTTS (last-transaction-timestamp) values embedded a comma that broke parsing across the whole CL Loan product. A permanent patch was in development (targeted for release by end of December 2022); in the interim, the workaround was to manually remove the comma from the LTTS timestamp field (e.g. change 'LTTS_15/02/2002, 16:00' to 'LTTS_15/02/2002 16:00') before reversing an LPT.
case_discussion: Q2 quickly identified the Salesforce locale-format change as the cause and gave the comma-removal workaround, with a permanent patch promised by year end.
current_status: Closed (31/12/2022) with a manual workaround in place pending the platform-wide patch.

subject: Investor Payout Error on LAI - 1007 & LAI - 870
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: On full-redemption payoffs of LAI-1007 (LPT-000011335) and LAI-870 (LPT-000011091), the entire LPT amount was applied to interest/principal/fees but no interest at all was paid out to investors, despite the investor payout job completing. This followed production changes made 01/02/2023 to enable Interest Posting on Investment Orders (IOs) and add InvestmentOrderInterestPostingDynamicJob to SOD/EOD processing.

Data-fix steps for the already-affected historic contracts were provided separately by email, to be tracked under a new case, since a first proposed historic-data-correction approach had to be scrapped and replaced.

current_status: Closed (03/06/2024) after patch (Loan 3.5054.223) release; residual historic data-fix work for already-affected contracts was to be tracked in a separate new case.

subject: Incorrect Data in Investment Orders
urgency: Intermittent
description: Three categories of bad Investment Order (IO) data found across live loans: (1) active IOs with £0 remaining investment amount, (2) inactive IOs that still show a remaining investment amount > 0, and (3) sold IOs that still show a remaining investment amount. Customer asked for root cause and data-fix steps, especially for active IOs.
issue_summary: Investment Order records across many contracts show remaining-investment-amount values inconsistent with their active/inactive/sold status, and the customer needed both an explanation and a data-fix path.
case_fix: Q2 confirmed category 3 (sold IOs retaining a remaining amount) is expected product behaviour. Categories 1 and 2 were traced to a bug in how the remaining investment amount is recalculated on loan payoff (when part of a payoff LPT is diverted to an auto-generated 'excess' LPT); a fix was released in Loan package 3.5054.177 (plus Common 3.5008.44, Marketplace 3.5003.2, JIRA PDRFF-1893) documented in release notes pages 12-13. Testing initially surfaced a regression (loans getting stuck as 'Active - Marked for Closure' with excess-LPT payoffs) traced to a payment-spread configuration difference between Dev and UAT orgs (Principal missing from the FOLK2FOLK Payment Spread in Dev), which the customer corrected locally; a further payout-shortfall side effect of the patch was asked to be tracked as its own case.
case_discussion: Long thread (Mar-Sep 2023): several workaround attempts for categories 1/2 (marking investors inactive, deleting/recreating ILT records) partially worked or introduced new null-object errors; multiple replication sessions and calls; a P1 bug (PDRFF-1893) was raised and patched; customer found a config-driven regression while testing the patch in Dev; category 3 was confirmed as expected and split into a separate case at closure.
current_status: Closed (07/09/2023) after the patch (Loan 3.5054.177) was released for categories 1/2; category 3 explicitly left as a new, separate case for any further concerns.

subject: Difference in Interest postings on Investment orders and Loan Contract
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Summed Investment Order (IO) interest postings show small penny-level differences from the corresponding loan-level interest posting (e.g. LAI-1091 in production; LAI-744 in UAT showed loan interest posting 3635 vs. summed IO postings 3635.04). Customer asked whether this is a rounding artifact or a configuration issue, and where to see unrounded amounts.
issue_summary: Aggregated Investment Order interest postings don't always exactly match the parent loan's interest posting, differing by a few pennies, raising a question of whether this is rounding or a bug.
case_fix: Q2's product team confirmed two distinct causes, both expected behaviour rather than bugs: (1) dividing and rounding shared interest across investors always produces small rounding differences (a rounding gain/loss versus a single loan-level figure), and (2) when an investor's shares are sold to a new investor, an internal 'interest rounding error' correction value is not carried over to the new investor, producing a one-off penny difference for that investor going forward. Q2 supplied a worked Excel example to document the mechanism; no code change was made.
case_discussion: Customer replicated the discrepancy in UAT/sandbox with specific contracts and provided detailed transaction histories; Q2 needed several months and internal product confirmation (including a JIRA PDRFF-2003 raised while investigating) before concluding both scenarios were by-design rounding behaviour; customer accepted the explanation and closed the case.
current_status: Closed (13/02/2024) - accepted as expected rounding/data-carryover behaviour, not a defect.

subject: Wrong payout of LPT cleared before due date for a delinquent loan
urgency: Constant
description: On delinquent loan LAI-712 (UAT), after a missed payment the next interest LPT (LPT-000002524, £1,435.41) was cleared before its due date, but the investor payout was only £717.67 - roughly half the amount collected. Customer reported the issue recurring regularly on delinquent loans paid early.
issue_summary: Clearing an interest payment early (before due date) on a loan that had previously gone delinquent caused the investor payout job to distribute significantly less than the amount actually collected.
case_fix: No permanent fix confirmed in the thread - Q2 could not replicate internally despite detailed replication steps provided by the customer and several call sessions; a bug (PDRFF-2414) was raised but subsequent Q2 upgrades changed conditions so the original replication steps stopped applying, and Q2 asked the customer to reconfirm replicability; case was closed with a customer satisfaction survey sent, without a confirmed shipped fix.
case_discussion: Extensive back-and-forth (May 2023-Mar 2024) with multiple Q2 support engineers rotating onto the case (Rohit Datta, Arturo Sanchez, Utkarsh Saxena, Jesus Diaz); customer provided step-by-step replication instructions and replicated it themselves multiple times, while Q2's internal environment could not reproduce it, requiring several live call sessions and log captures; a JIRA bug was raised (PDRFF-2414) but no confirmed patch is recorded before closure.
current_status: Closed (07/03/2024); root cause was accepted as a genuine but hard-to-reproduce bug (PDRFF-2414) - no confirmed fix delivery recorded in this case's thread.

subject: Payout not happening correctly to exited investor after IO Sell
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: When an Investment Order (IO) is sold to a replacement investor mid-period (e.g. LAI-1134: Roger & Gillian Thorn's IO sold to Gillian Mary Thorn on 29/03/2023), the interest accrued before the sale (21/03-29/03/2023, ~£28.89) was never paid out to the exiting investor, while the new investor correctly received interest for their own holding period. Same pattern seen on LAI-880, 1048, 1124 - believed linked to enabling Interest Posting on IOs.
issue_summary: After an Investment Order is sold mid-period, the exiting investor's pre-sale accrued interest is lost instead of being paid out, across multiple contracts.
case_fix: Q2 raised JIRA PDRFF-2178 and released an initial patch (Loan 3.5054.191, per release notes p.24) in September 2023 to address the missing payout; testing then surfaced a secondary distribution issue (how the LPT interest amount is split between the sold IO and the new IO, governed by the formula Interest portion = LPT Interest × (interestCalculatedForInvestor / interestCalculatedForBorrower)); a further patch (Loan 3.5054.223, release notes p.44) was released in May 2024, plus supporting packages, to address the remaining distribution logic; a suggested workaround using IO Priority Scores was later found to have its own issues, which the product team was still addressing at case closure.
case_discussion: Year-long investigation with multiple replications, log captures, and calls; customer pushed back when Q2's explanation of a 'secondary issue' lacked detail; Q2 explained the underlying interest-split formula and confirmed the split behaviour (not full transfer to the new investor) is by design once a patch is applied; case was closed after 2+ weeks of no response following the second patch, with an invitation to reopen if issues persisted.
current_status: Closed (11/06/2024) after two rounds of patches (Loan 3.5054.191 then 3.5054.223); a known issue with the Priority-Score-based workaround remained under product review at closure.

subject: 0.003p to excess on Management Fee in Production
urgency: Intermittent
description: A £250 Management Fee charge (CHG-00007171 on LAI-1297) was split across two LPTs (250 and 0.00) for March, then in April clearing the next LPT only applied 249.99 to the charge, leaving a 0.003-penny excess instead of the fee being fully satisfied by a single £250 LPT. At least 4 contracts/charges affected.
issue_summary: Management Fee charges intermittently leave a fractional-penny amount unsatisfied and routed to 'excess' instead of being cleanly paid off by the corresponding LPT.
case_fix: Root cause: the custom F2FUpdatePeriodicFeeBatch class wasn't setting the charge's 'Paid to charge' flag correctly when an LPT fully satisfied it, so the next LPT tried to satisfy a near-zero remaining balance (0.01-type penny amounts), compounding into an 'excess' entry. Q2 made a targeted code change to F2FUpdatePeriodicFeeBatch (line 117 area), tested it in Preprod on the 4 known affected contracts, confirmed it worked, and had the customer roll it out; the same issue resurfaced over a year later (Oct 2024) on LAI-938, at which point Q2 closed this case and asked for a new one referencing it rather than continuing the old thread.
case_discussion: Q2 initially could not replicate in Dev; customer supplied the specific affected LAI/charge list; Q2 traced it to the periodic-fee batch class, proposed and tested a code fix with the customer in Preprod across all four affected contracts, then rolled it to production; a recurrence over a year later was directed to a new case rather than reopening this one.
current_status: Closed (18/10/2024, reopened once then re-closed) - original fix delivered via a code change to F2FUpdatePeriodicFeeBatch; a recurrence on a new contract was pointed to a fresh case.

subject: Interest payout issue on LPT-000018134 in LAI -1229
description: A principal payment due 21/07/2023 on LAI-1229 (LPT-000018134) failed with a 'Duplicate id' error referencing an interest posting transaction. A retry of the payout job on 24/07/2023 succeeded. Customer asked for the root cause and whether running the payout job alongside an interest posting transaction on the same day could cause this.
issue_summary: A one-off 'Duplicate id' exception blocked an investor payout on the due date, but the same payout succeeded a few days later on retry, with no clear cause identified from the available logs.
case_fix: No fix identified - Q2's product team reviewed but could not determine an exact root cause from the batch process log/stack trace available for this one-off occurrence, and asked the customer to raise a new case with fresh logs if it recurred. Q2 later folded this case as a 'child' reference under a newer case for ongoing tracking.
case_discussion: Q2 acknowledged, investigated the stack trace, found it insufficient to pinpoint the cause, and asked whether it could be closed with a note to reopen (via new case) if it recurred; customer accepted, asking at least for the general conditions under which such an error can occur.
current_status: Closed (11/08/2023) as an unreplicated one-off; linked as a child reference to a newer, related case for future tracking.

subject: Investor payout issue in production
description: Investor payout job failed in production due to a duplicate id error.
issue_summary: Investor payout job failed with a 'Duplicate id' DML error because an overlapping previous-month and current-month LPT were both trying to reverse the same ILTID (ILTID-0000151963), caused by July's IPT not having been paid before running the payout job.
case_fix: Marked the relevant Fees LPT (LPT-000017913) as 'PAID TO INVESTOR' to resolve the conflict; Q2 advised that when clearing prior-month and current-month payments on the same day, Fee records should be marked Paid to Investor first, before running the payout job, to avoid recurrence.
case_discussion: Follow-up to case 03727480. Q2 investigated the stack trace (Class.loan.SecureDML.updateRecords chain) and identified the duplicate-id root cause; provided the workaround and general process guidance to prevent future occurrences.
current_status: Closed - resolved via data fix (marking LPT as Paid to Investor); process guidance given to prevent recurrence.

subject: Past Maturity Rescheduling
description: Rescheduling a loan on its maturity date to a higher rate (a Folk2Folk business requirement) moves 'Interest Posted' to 'Interest Remaining', causing any later interest payment to route to 'Excess' instead of clearing correctly.
issue_summary: No product workaround exists for correctly applying interest payments after a past-maturity-date reschedule to a higher rate; payments intended to clear interest post to Excess instead.
case_fix: No direct fix delivered as a workaround; Q2 raised Inquiry JIRA PDRFF-2724 for a product enhancement, tentatively targeted for the December 2024 release. Case closed on that ETA-only commitment.
case_discussion: Q2 initially closed the case in Nov 2023 stating there was no workaround and it required a design change; customer pushed back and case was reopened; Q2 (with Bhanupriya Sharma, Vishal Lakkammanavar, Rohit Datta involved) then raised the enhancement JIRA and gave a tentative release ETA.
current_status: Closed - no workaround; enhancement (PDRFF-2724) tentatively planned for December 2024 release, accepted by customer as the resolution path.

subject: Investor payout job failed in production for LAI-1027
description: Investor payout job failed in production for loan LAI-1027.
issue_summary: Payout job failure traced to two issues: a locale date-time conversion error ('String to Datetime conversion logic for Locale en_GB is not available', same family as cases 03549948/03600246) and a missing Last Interest Accrual Date / missing certificate-rate-change transaction date on an Investment Order.
case_fix: Data-fixed the missing transaction date and Last Interest Accrual Date, then reran the IO Interest Accrual job before the payout job; verified via a targeted Apex script run through Database.executeBatch.
case_discussion: Q2 diagnosed both the locale bug and the missing-date data issue; a related DAG-job execution problem surfaced during investigation and was split off into a new case, 03756673.
current_status: Closed - resolved via data fix and job rerun; related DAG job issue tracked separately under case 03756673.

subject: Unable to Run Dag Jobs from Servicing Configuration
description: Unable to run DAG jobs from Servicing Configuration; split off from case 03752490 during investigation of a payout job failure.
issue_summary: Running any DAG job from Servicing Configuration threw 'clcommon:Too many query rows: 50001' in DynamicJobAPIImpl.checkIsDagRunning, because the clcommon__Job_Logging__c object had accumulated over 50,000 records, breaking the row-count check used to detect a running DAG job.
case_fix: Resolved operationally by archiving/purging old DAG job-logging records to bring clcommon__Job_Logging__c back under the query-row limit; JIRA PDRFF-2450 raised for a proper code-level fix (row-limit-safe check) since the underlying issue could recur as logs grow again.
case_discussion: Q2 (Deeptha S with Rayapati Sarath Teja) identified the row-count governor limit as the cause; closed together with a referenced related case (03834406) per an internal email chain quoted in the comments.
current_status: Closed - resolved by archiving old job-logging records; code fix tracked via PDRFF-2450; see related case 03834406.

subject: The distribution of investor funds for LAI-00001289 was halted
description: Payout for LPT-000019817 (LAI-1289) could not be processed; no interest was posted on the last due date (02/09/2023) even though the IO Interest Accrual and Posting job had run; the interest posting date on the IO had unexpectedly changed to 28/09/2023.
issue_summary: Payout blocked because interest was not posted correctly on LAI-1289's IO; investigation found unexplained manual updates to the contract history (Next Due Date/Payment Amount/Next Due Generation Date changed on 22/08/2023) that had shifted dates, and the IP had actually posted correctly but the payout amounts calculated were incorrect.
case_fix: Q2 (Rayapati Sarath Teja) data-corrected the contract, updating the interest posted and excess values to reflect the correct figures after discussing on a call.
case_discussion: Multiple back-and-forth exchanges to pin down whether interest had posted; Q2 found manual contract-history edits with no attributable user; a call was held to align on the fix approach before Q2 applied the correction.
current_status: Closed - resolved via manual data correction of interest posted/excess values on the contract.

subject: Sold Investment Orders
urgency: Medium – 3: There is an impact to your business, but your business continues to function
description: Behaviour of Sold Investment Orders unclear/incorrect: when an IO is fully sold, Remaining Investment Amount does not update to £0; when partially sold, a new IO is created for the continuation of the original. F2F expects a sold IO to show no remaining investment amount since another investor now holds it.
issue_summary: Two scenarios raised: (1) fully sold IOs don't zero out Remaining Investment Amount (confirmed as a bug), and (2) partially sold IOs create a new IO for the seller's continuing position (confirmed as expected/by-design behaviour, no change planned).
case_fix: Q2 converted the fully-sold-IO scenario to a Bug and provided patches (Loan 3.5054.212, Marketplace 3.5003.6, Common 3.5008.44) so Remaining Investment Amount zeroes out and the sold amount appears in a Paid field; fix applies to new contracts only, a data fix is needed for pre-existing contracts. The partial-sale/new-IO behaviour was confirmed as intentional design with no change made.
case_discussion: Extended discussion and calls over several months (Sept 2023-March 2024) clarifying requirements via an attached document, JIRA conversion from Inquiry to Bug, and ETA slips (19 Feb 2024 → 11 Mar 2024) due to reprioritization against another F2F JIRA.
current_status: Closed - patch delivered for fully-sold IO scenario (data fix needed for old contracts); partial-sale behaviour confirmed as no-change/by-design.

subject: Calculations for Daily interest Accrual on CLS
description: Customer's manual calculation of daily interest accrual (Principal Remaining * Rate / 360 * Days) for LAI-911 did not match CLS's figure (manual £586.81 vs CLS £586.80), with the mismatch starting on day 21; asked Q2 to clarify CLS's rounding method.
issue_summary: Discrepancy between manually-calculated and CLS-calculated daily interest accrual figures for LAI-911, apparently due to a rounding-method difference; also asked whether partial redemption is supported.
case_fix: Q2 explained CLS's interest-rounding methodology on a call; confirmed no partial-redemption feature exists in the product — for full payoff, customer should generate a payoff quote and create a payoff transaction instead.
case_discussion: Resolved via a single explanatory call; no code or data change was needed, purely a clarification of existing calculation/rounding logic and payoff process.
current_status: Closed - explanation provided; no product change required.

subject: Historic data correction for investor payout issues
description: F2F needed to produce annual investor interest statements and had found several historic payout discrepancies in production (per cases 03515883, 03692256, 03594592); requested guidance on the best approach to correct these historic data issues across many investment orders.
issue_summary: No systematic way existed to bulk-correct historic payout/interest-posting discrepancies spanning three separate root causes (IO sale payout issue, no interest payout on full redemption, LPT payout mismatched to interest component) across dozens of listed LPT/LAI records.
case_fix: Q2 raised PDRFF-2519 and CSE-457 to work out a data-fix approach; ultimately F2F decided to correct the April 2023-2024 data themselves outside the system and generate PDFs for the Investor Portal rather than have Q2 correct it in-system; Q2's support was still needed for any incorrect payouts from 5 April 2024 onward.
case_discussion: Long multi-month exchange providing detailed lists of affected LPT/LAI record pairs across the three underlying issues; multiple calls scheduled; ultimately closed on F2F's decision to self-correct historic statement data rather than pursue an in-system fix for the affected period.
current_status: Closed - F2F opted to correct 2023-2024 statement data outside the system; future (post 5 Apr 2024) payout errors to be handled via new cases.

subject: Payout Issues in LAI-1418 & LAI-00000723 Following Production Data Correction for IO
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Payout discrepancy in production for LPT-000020796 of LAI-1418: paid amount lower than the LPT amount, following an earlier production data correction on the IO. LAI-00000723 was later added as a related affected contract (case 03801864 was closed as a duplicate and merged into this one).
issue_summary: After production IO data correction, full payoff/payout jobs distributed excess interest incorrectly (root cause: excess payoff IPT amount not allocated to investors because next investor interest posting date on the IO side was set ahead of the payoff, so the excess payoff IPT wasn't created on the investor side); issue could not be replicated in UAT/Pre-Prod for a long time.
case_fix: Q2 eventually delivered a patch (Utilities/FileGen/Common/Integration/Loan 3.5054.223/Marketplace/Notify packages) released mid-May 2024; also provided manual replication/data-fix steps and confirmed the fix via release notes; case closed after no further response confirming remaining issues.
case_discussion: Long troubleshooting effort (Oct 2023-Jun 2024) including repeated failed replication attempts in UAT/Pre-Prod, multiple calls, LMA access issues, and eventual root-cause identification tied to investor-side excess IPT allocation; patch delayed several times before release.
current_status: Closed - patch released and applied; case closed after no further customer response on outstanding issues.

subject: Payout discrepancies after IO Data correction
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: After a production IO data correction (from case 03515883), LAI-1299's partial redemption on 1/9/23 caused £18.06 of additional interest to be spread incorrectly across all existing investors instead of being paid to the investor entitled to it (Anita Evans); her IO's interest remaining was increased then reduced by the same £18.06.
issue_summary: Sold IOs kept incorrectly accruing/receiving payout of interest after being sold, mainly affecting LAI-755 and later ~10 other partial-redemption-affected contracts, because Interest Posted on the sold IO remained non-zero so payout jobs continued to include it.
case_fix: Q2 (Utkarsh Saxena) advised setting the Interest Posted field to 0 on affected sold IOs (same data-fix steps as related case 03824216) to stop erroneous ongoing payouts; customer applied this and confirmed payouts stopped, after which the case was closed; the related interest-accrual-on-sold-IO issue was tracked under a separate case with the product team.
case_discussion: Extensive multi-month investigation (Oct 2023-Jun 2024) involving JIRA raised for the product team, an Excel data sheet of affected contracts/ILIDs/before-after values, several calls, and iterative confirmation across multiple sold-IO contracts before the Interest Posted = 0 workaround was confirmed effective.
current_status: Closed - resolved via setting Interest Posted to 0 on sold IOs; broader interest-accrual-on-sold-IO fix tracked in a separate case.

subject: Investor Fee Payout discrepancies in Production
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Full redemption of LAI-1047 on 16/10/2023 included a fee charge of 39.27, but investor payout for the fee only totalled 14.07; root cause traced to fee distribution being calculated on the original share percentage rather than current share.
issue_summary: Fee payout on full redemption under-distributed to investors because fee-share calculation used the original investment share percentage instead of the correct/current one; unresolved by an attempted sandbox fix that tried prioritizing Active IOs.
case_fix: Q2 replicated the issue, raised PDRFF-2560, and released a patch (Utilities/FileGen/Common/Integration/Loan 3.5054.207/Marketplace/Notify packages) in Feb 2024; case closed a month after release confirmation.
case_discussion: Root cause replicated internally; JIRA raised; patch delayed from initial ETA to Feb 2024 with release notes eventually supplied on request.
current_status: Closed - resolved via product patch correcting fee-share distribution calculation.

subject: Investor Interest Payout Error on LAI-00000723
description: Full redemption LPT-000021684 on LAI-00000723 (transaction date 20/10/2023) paid out only £249.98 total interest to investors when the LPT carried an interest amount of £427.06.
issue_summary: Same root cause as case 03780458 - excess payoff interest posting not handled properly so the final interest wasn't fully spread to investors on full redemption.
case_fix: No separate fix; Q2 confirmed this was the same scenario as case 03780458 and merged/tracked the contract there instead.
case_discussion: Q2 (Rayapati Sarath Teja) identified the duplicate nature on a call with the customer and closed this case in favor of consolidated tracking under 03780458.
current_status: Closed as Duplicate - tracked under case 03780458.

subject: Payout Discrepancy in Interest Allocation for LPT-21943 of LAI-1259
description: LPT-000021943 on LAI-1259 (transaction date 27/10/2023, amount £3,927.08, fully towards interest) resulted in investor payouts totalling £4,304.33 - more than the amount received from the borrower.
issue_summary: Investor payout exceeded the amount actually received because of incorrect IO interest posting after a certificate rate change; confirmed as a duplicate root cause of case 03823980 (backdated certificate rate change causing incorrect interest accrual on IO).
case_fix: Closed as duplicate of case 03823980 once Q2 confirmed the same backdated-certificate-rate-change root cause; the patch delivered under 03823980 covers this issue too. PDRFF-2660 was raised for the IO posting inaccuracy before the duplicate link was confirmed.
case_discussion: Q2 replicated internally, initially raised a separate JIRA (PDRFF-2660), then identified the case as a duplicate of 03823980 and pointed to the patch already released there.
current_status: Closed as Duplicate of case 03823980; resolved via that case's patch.

subject: IO Sale issue on Production org
description: IO sale on LAI-1329 (investor JOA00001651 selling to ROD00003804 for £13,810.80) created incorrect resulting IOs: the seller's IO wasn't fully sold/closed and retained a lower-amount active IO tied to a same-day partial redemption, while the buyer's new IO also had an incorrect Principal Paid value instead of £0.
issue_summary: When an IO sale and a partial redemption occur on the same day, the system processes the sale before the redemption (rather than after), causing the new IOs created by the sale to inherit a non-zero Principal Paid proportional to share percentage - which F2F disputes as incorrect, since the buyer never actually had principal repaid to them.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) determined this is expected product behaviour under the current design (IO treated as an instrument; number of shares fixed at IO creation) and declined to patch it, citing risk to existing behaviour; raised it as a roadmap enhancement (tentative ETA December 2024) and recommended F2F implement a customisation in the interim; a related sub-issue (new investor incorrectly showing Principal Paid) was tracked via PDRFF-2652/PDRFF-2971 as an Improvement, not a bug fix.
case_discussion: Long-running dispute (Nov 2023-Aug 2024) with detailed worked examples from both sides; Henri Street repeatedly challenged Q2's 'expected behaviour' explanation with concrete share-price and principal-paid worked examples showing it produces incorrect results; Q2 ultimately held its design position and pushed the fix to a future release/customisation rather than a patch.
current_status: Closed - Q2 maintains this is expected design behaviour; enhancement tentatively targeted for December 2024 release; customer advised to pursue a customisation in the meantime.

subject: Unable to make date movement in Pre-Prod
description: After syncing Pre-Prod with Production, date movement (Start Next Day / Move To Date) in Servicing Configuration > SOD/EOD Process failed with 'clcommon:Too many query rows: 50001' in DynamicJobAPIImpl.checkIsDagRunning, blocking use of the org entirely.
issue_summary: Same governor-limit family issue as case 03756673: the DAG-running check query exceeded 50,000 rows, this time because several InvestorPayoutDynamicJob batch executions were stuck in 'PROCESSING' status in clcommon__Dag_Logging__c after the Pre-Prod/Production sync.
case_fix: Q2 (Deeptha S) queried for stuck-processing DAG logging records and aborted them, then confirmed date movement worked again after moving the system date forward.
case_discussion: JIRA raised by Bhanupriya Sharma for tracking; resolved operationally by identifying and aborting the stuck DAG log records rather than a code patch.
current_status: Closed - resolved by aborting stuck DAG logging records; date movement confirmed working.

subject: Incorrect Interest Payout on LAI-766
description: Interest payout LPT-000022876 on LAI-00000766 (transaction date 20/11/2023) distributed only £422.68 to investors in total though the LPT carried an interest amount of £425.82.
issue_summary: Discrepancy explained as a legitimate 1-day interest accrual difference between the contract-level rate (9%, changed 18/10) and the investor-level certificate rate (7%, changed 19/10) - not a bug but a timing mismatch between when the contract rate change and certificate rate change transactions were dated.
case_fix: No fix required; Q2 (Deeptha S) provided a detailed reconciliation calculation for each investor proving the payout was mathematically consistent with the 1-day rate-timing difference, which the customer accepted.
case_discussion: Q2 walked through per-investor ratio calculations on a call to demonstrate the shortfall exactly matched the expected 1-day interest differential; customer accepted the explanation and approved closure.
current_status: Closed - explained as expected behaviour from a 1-day rate-change timing difference; no fix needed.

subject: Issues Arising from Interest Accrual Due to Backdated Certificate Rate Change in IO
description: Incorrect payout on LAI-00001134 (21/11/2023) traced to erroneous interest accrual on IOs caused by a backdated certificate rate change - the loan was rescheduled on 14/11 with a backdated transaction date of 4/11, and the IO certificate rate change was similarly backdated to 4/11.
issue_summary: Backdating a certificate rate change transaction date caused all related IOs to double-accrue interest for the backdated period, leading to incorrect (inflated) investor payouts; confirmed to recur on other loans (e.g. LAI-763) with the same backdating pattern.
case_fix: Q2 raised PDRFF-2205 (shared with case 03814520) and released a patch (Utilities/FileGen/Common/Integration/Loan 3.5054.207/Marketplace/Notify) in Feb 2024; case closed a month after release confirmation.
case_discussion: Customer reported a second occurrence on LAI-763 while awaiting the fix; Q2 initially couldn't see backdating on the flagged ILIDs and asked for clarification; patch delivered against a Feb 19 ETA with an acknowledged short delay.
current_status: Closed - resolved via product patch (PDRFF-2205) preventing double interest accrual on backdated certificate rate changes.

subject: Accrual of Interest on Sold IO
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Full redemption of LAI-922 on 17/11/2023 included interest paid to an investor who had sold their IO back in August; IO history showed interest continuing to accrue on the IO after it was sold.
issue_summary: Sold IOs kept accruing interest after sale whenever an Interest Payout LPT or Fee LPT was later picked up by the investor payout job, affecting roughly 80-90 ILIDs in production that met specific conditions (mid-month sale, Income to be Collected flag true, prior to an earlier related patch PDRFF-2178).
case_fix: Q2 raised PDRFF-2807, provided a query to identify affected ILIDs plus manual data-fix steps for existing bad records, and released a code patch (Loan 3.5054.227 + dependent packages) in June 2024 to stop future accrual on already-sold IOs going forward.
case_discussion: Extended multi-month investigation (Nov 2023-Jul 2024) including internal replication difficulty, detailed SOQL queries to isolate ~80-90 affected ILIDs, a manual data-fix document, and a code patch; customer flagged specific ILID examples (e.g. ILID 8188, ILID-0000010941) to help narrow the pattern.
current_status: Closed - resolved via PDRFF-2807 patch plus manual data-fix steps for previously affected sold IOs.

subject: Incorrect Payout after IO Sale
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Even after the patch from case 03692256, LAI-1042 still mispaid following an IO sale: after ILID-0000004893 sold its IO on 04/12, a £2,708.33 payment produced a £2,719.24 payout, with the sold investor receiving 32 days of interest (£173.33) instead of the correct 30 days (£162.50) - payout exceeding the borrower payment.
issue_summary: When a backdated payment is cleared after an IO sale and payout runs the same day, the system gave the sold investor priority in interest posting/payout ahead of other investors, resulting in an over-payment; product concluded backdated payments cannot be fully supported after an IO sale under current design.
case_fix: Q2 (Deeptha S) shipped a patch (Loan 3.5054.223 / Marketplace 3.5003.8, released mid-May 2024, PDRFF-2793/ND-7690) changing payout behavior so the sold investor's interest is capped as of the LPT transaction date rather than taking priority, while advising as a best practice to run investor payout for the prior LPT before performing an IO sale; a related regression (LPT reversal not correctly updating sold IOs) was found during testing and flagged as a caution rather than blocking closure.
case_discussion: Long replication effort (Dec 2023-Jun 2024) with multiple failed internal replication attempts, several rounds of sandbox/UAT reproduction with detailed scenario steps, product-team design discussions on how backdated-payment-after-sale scenarios should behave, and eventual patch release and sandbox testing sign-off.
current_status: Closed - resolved via patch (PDRFF-2793/ND-7690) after sandbox testing; caution noted regarding a related LPT-reversal-on-sold-IO regression still being fixed separately.

subject: No Investor Loan Transaction generated after Investor Payout
description: Interest payment LPT-000023095 (£814.58) on LAI-1239, cleared 05/12/23, had its investor payout job complete on 06/12/2023 but no Investor Loan Transaction records were generated; a manual data correction was applied in the meantime.
issue_summary: Root cause traced to loan__Contractual_Due_Day__c: when a contract matures, the next interest posting date on the IO is derived from the contractual (original) due day rather than the current due day, so for LAI-1239 (contractual due day 10) the next posting date rolled to 10/12 instead of the actual 05/12, causing the payout job to skip generating the ILT.
case_fix: Q2 (Deeptha S) identified the discrepancy via a SOQL query isolating active contracts where contractual and current due days differed (found 2 of 44 checked: LAI-1239 and LAI-1379) and had the customer manually correct the next interest posting dates on the affected IOs; also raised an internal Salesforce case to rule out an org-level job execution conflict.
case_discussion: Root-cause explanation given after several calls; customer applied the manual fix themselves and confirmed no other production examples were found; case closed alongside related case 03756673 in the same email thread.
current_status: Closed - resolved via manual correction of next interest posting dates on the two affected IOs; enable history tracking recommended to monitor for recurrence.

subject: Application department is not getting created in DEV sandbox
description: After updating existing departments and tasks (renaming, order change, etc.), a new department was no longer being generated under Application on creation in the DEV sandbox.
issue_summary: Application department creation was silently failing after department/task configuration changes; customer's own investigation found orphaned department members (department members with no department) in the system.
case_fix: Customer self-resolved by querying and deleting the orphaned department member records, after which application departments began generating correctly again; no Q2-side code change was needed.
case_discussion: Q2 offered a call to discuss remaining questions after the workaround; a separate follow-up case was planned for fixing existing apps affected by the department/task config changes.
current_status: Closed - resolved by customer deleting orphaned department member records; follow-up case planned for existing-app fixes.

subject: Resolution of February and March Payment Issue for Loans with Due Dates Beyond the 28th
description: Follow-up to case 03542537: for loans with due dates of 29, 30, or 31 using the 'Months and Days' time counting method with interest-only actual behaviour, the February and March repayment amounts differ from the rest of the schedule (e.g. LAI-1200); asked for a workaround to keep them consistent.
issue_summary: With 'Months and Days' time counting, February's shorter 28/29-day length and March's 31-day length naturally produce different interest amounts than the standard 30-day months for loans due on the 29th-31st - confirmed as expected system behaviour, not a bug, affecting roughly 130 active-investor contracts.
case_fix: No product fix; Q2 (Shalini Panjavarnam) proposed three workarounds - reschedule with a different due day, reschedule specifying a whole-number interest-only payment amount (with a decimal shortfall absorbed in the final month), or manually editing the payment amount fields - but the customer found none of these feasible for their contracts, and Q2's product team ultimately confirmed no other workaround exists.
case_discussion: Extensive multi-week exploration of workaround options including sandbox date-movement testing (with a leap-year note that 2020 could substitute for 2024 testing), before Q2's product team confirmed the Feb/March variance is inherent to the Months-and-Days calculation method.
current_status: Closed - confirmed as expected product behaviour with no available workaround; case closed on that basis.

subject: Process of correcting existing applications after changing Departments and Tasks in CL Originate
description: After changing Departments and Tasks configuration under Originate, F2F needed a way to correct in-flight applications: reassigning owners when a department was removed, moving apps stuck in a removed department to the next one, handling new tasks added to existing departments, and tracking completed vs remaining tasks under the new config.
issue_summary: Department/task configuration changes only apply cleanly to new applications; in-flight applications require manual or scripted remediation, and changing an application's department ID alone does not release its next task unless the Application Owner is also re-set (and only certain user profiles trigger correct task release).
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) confirmed the design limitation, provided a workaround (release the application to queue then reassign the same owner) and worked with the customer's CK team to build and refine an Apex script (raised as Inquiry JIRA PDRFF-2822) to bulk-remap application department IDs and complete outstanding tasks; script was optimized after hitting a 'Too many SOQL queries: 101' governor-limit error, then successfully run against all production applications.
case_discussion: Multi-month iterative effort (Jan-May 2024) building and testing a remediation script across sandbox/pre-prod/production, including a governor-limit fix and confirmation the owner-reassignment step was required for task release; case held open an extra week post-fix to confirm production stability before closing.
current_status: Closed - resolved via a custom script (per PDRFF-2822) that remaps department IDs and releases tasks for existing applications; confirmed stable in production.

subject: Amendment of lookup type search box
description: Requested that the Investment Order (IO) sale lookup search box allow searching by just first or last name instead of requiring the investor's full name, with a dropdown of matches.
issue_summary: The IO Sale 'Buyer Account' field is a lookup on the standard Account object (single Name field, so search must start from the full/starting name), unlike Contact lookups which combine separate First Name and Last Name fields for more flexible matching - this is standard Salesforce object behaviour, not a bug.
case_fix: No fix delivered/needed; Q2 explained the Account vs Contact lookup behaviour difference as inherent Salesforce design, and the customer confirmed the issue was resolved/accepted on their end.
case_discussion: Straightforward explanatory exchange; customer accepted the explanation and approved closure.
current_status: Closed - explained as standard Salesforce Account-lookup behaviour; no change made.

subject: Interest Postings for Investors Issue where IO Sale/Principal Payment occurs day before Posting Date
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: LPT-000025902 on LAI-00001393 paid ILID-0000008377 £541.67 instead of the expected £533.55: a partial redemption of £45,000 occurred on 9 Feb (day before the 10th posting date), but interest posted on the IO the next day as if the full £100,000 were still outstanding for all 30 days, rather than accruing the last day at the reduced £55,000 balance, so the Contract-level and IO-level interest posted amounts didn't match.
issue_summary: The overnight batch job normally 'unaccrues' interest for the day to reflect a lower Remaining Investment Amount, but this doesn't happen correctly when the principal payment clearing and the IO posting job occur on the same day, causing IO-level interest to overstate what the contract actually accrued.
case_fix: Q2 (Prajwal Kumar D, with Raghu) proposed running the Investor Payout job twice daily - once around 10 PM before the normal EOD/SOD chaining, and once as part of the regular process - so same-day partial redemptions are captured correctly before the standard job runs; customer instead opted to build their own customization to detect a partial redemption the day before and run a targeted payout job just for that specific LPT rather than doubling the daily job for everyone.
case_discussion: Extended discussion (Mar-May 2024) including a raised PDRFF, clarification that Q2's proposed twice-daily job would not double-pay already-processed LPTs, and F2F's concern about doubling the number of investor payout files needing reconciliation each day, leading them to choose a narrower custom workaround over Q2's general one.
current_status: Closed - customer implemented a targeted workaround (running payout specifically for identified same-day-redemption LPTs) instead of Q2's twice-daily job proposal.

subject: LAI - 910 Data issue
description: LAI-910 posted 3x its monthly interest (£42,900 instead of £14,300) on 9 March; this followed an earlier automatic-rescheduling-from-bad-to-good-standing issue that had left extra non-due interest posted on the loan, which had since been fixed but left the underlying data uncorrected.
issue_summary: Root cause traced to a manual change of the 'reversed' flag on several LPTs on 06/03/2024: reversing LPT-000023203 (which carried an RTA, unlike the others) shifted the last accrual date back two months (09/12/2023 instead of 09/02/2024), doubling the accrual amount (£12,870 → £41,470); when the other LPTs' reverse flags were subsequently reset and LPT-000026971 cleared, Interest Remaining and Interest Accrued combined incorrectly, producing the tripled £42,900 posting on 9 March.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) had the customer reverse LPT-000026971 and LPT-000026726, run the Investor Payout reversal job, mark IPT-00012303 as paid with corrected Interest Posted/Due Amount of £14,300, and review IR/Interest Posted/Interest Accrued values on the contract; confirmed data-fixed after a call.
case_discussion: Detailed forensic reconstruction of the exact sequence of manual reverse-flag changes and their cascading effect on accrual dates and amounts; resolved via targeted data correction rather than a code fix, since the root cause was manual LPT flag manipulation.
current_status: Closed - resolved via manual data correction (LPT reversals and Interest Posted/Due Amount correction) after root-cause analysis of manual reverse-flag changes.

subject: Getting an error while funding a Loan Application in Production Org
description: Funding loan application APP-00001334 (100% in funding) threw a FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION ('Please select whether the Address is a Current or Previous Address') from a custom Address-object validation rule, triggered inside clcommon.AccountTrigger's afterUpdate/copyStandardObjectAddressToCommonAddress logic; the same funding action did not reproduce the error in pre-production.
issue_summary: A recently added F2F validation rule on the Address object conflicted with the managed package's AccountTrigger logic that copies standard-object address data to the common Address object during funding, causing the funding operation to fail in production only.
case_fix: Not fully detailed in the case comments beyond Q2 requesting managed-package logs and confirmation of scope (single application vs. all); case was owned and closed by the customer's own contact (Anup Kumar Biswas), suggesting the issue was resolved on the customer side, likely by adjusting or exempting the new Address validation rule for the trigger's automated updates.
case_discussion: Q2 asked whether the error was isolated to one application and requested a call plus package logs to investigate the trigger-vs-validation-rule conflict.
current_status: Closed - resolved (details of final fix not fully documented in case comments; likely an adjustment to the custom Address validation rule).

subject: Investor Payout not generated for LAI-1483
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Follow-up to case 03834406: multiple contracts (LAI-1483, LAI-1352, LAI-1488, LAI-1257) had their IO-side interest posting date diverge from the loan contract's, so investor payout did not occur as expected; asked what causes the IO's Next Investor Interest Posting Date to change.
issue_summary: When a contract crosses maturity without being rescheduled first, and the Current Due Day differs from the original Due Day at funding time, the contract's Next Interest Posting Date incorrectly used the (unchanging) Due Day rather than Current Due Day; separately, rescheduling a contract updates the contract's Next Interest Posting Date but does NOT update the corresponding Next Investor Interest Posting Date on the IO, leaving it stuck on a stale date (sometimes far in the future, e.g. 31/12/3000) so investor-side posting/payout never triggers.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) replicated the issue internally via a detailed multi-step scenario (contract creation, funding-stage manual date fields, rescheduling before/after maturity) and released a patch (Loan 3.5054.227 + dependent packages) in June 2024 to keep the IO's Next Investor Interest Posting Date in sync with contract rescheduling.
case_discussion: Q2 initially pushed back that this looked like a data/process issue tied to manual field changes and rescheduling after maturity date rather than a bug, requesting exact replication steps; after internal replication succeeded, it was accepted as a genuine bug and patched; case closed a month after no further response following the patch release.
current_status: Closed - resolved via product patch keeping IO-side Next Investor Interest Posting Date synchronized with contract rescheduling.

subject: Sold Investment Orders Patch issue
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: While testing the patch delivered for case 03767970 (Sold Investment Orders), found that the 'Total Amount Paid' field on a fully-sold IO (ILID-0000001690, in F2F Dev sandbox) was not updating as expected.
issue_summary: Q2 explained Total Amount Paid only updates when there is an actual Principal payment on the IO; since the test contract was interest-only, there was no principal payment to reflect - this is expected behaviour, not a defect in the patch. Separately, the customer argued that selling an IO should logically move the sold amount into Principal Paid the same way a redemption does, which Q2 agreed to raise but treated as a new ask rather than a patch defect.
case_fix: For fully sold IOs, a further patch (Marketplace 3.5003.11, released Sept 2024) was delivered so Principal Paid updates correctly on full sale; for partially sold IOs, the same behaviour was deferred and bundled into a future Partial-IO enhancement rather than fixed here.
case_discussion: Long-running case (Mar-Oct 2024) with repeated customer follow-ups over multi-month silences (Stephanie Skinner noted '3 months with no update'); Q2 repeatedly reiterated the Total Amount Paid explanation before ultimately delivering the fully-sold-IO fix and pushing partial-sale handling to a future enhancement.
current_status: Closed - fully-sold IO Principal Paid behaviour fixed via patch; partially-sold IO handling deferred to a future enhancement.

subject: Payout mismatch on LPT-000027563 of LAI-1432 in production
description: Payout on LPT-000027563 (LAI-1432) paid investors less than the LPT amount.
issue_summary: Root cause was a manual February-month interest data fix (IPT-00012688 changed from £5,112.85 to £4,947.92, contract Interest Posted reduced from £6,154.52 to £5,989.59) that was later inadvertently reversed when a backdated Fee LPT (transaction date 29/02/2024) was cleared on 03/04/2024, recalculating interest and restoring the contract's Interest Posted back to £6,154.52 while the investor-side Actual Interest Posted retained the February data-fix value - the resulting mismatch between contract-level and investor-level interest fed into the payout-share formula and produced an incorrect (lower) investor payout for two consecutive months.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) provided a detailed RCA with exact IPT-level calculations and a data-fix procedure: reduce the current contract Interest Posted by one day, correct IPT-00012770's Interest Posted/Paid to £4,947.92, and adjust the amount paid on the subsequent IPT-00013233; also advised avoiding further backdated payments/reversals around the fix date. Confirmed as a data-fix scenario stemming from the February correction, not a patchable bug.
case_discussion: Extensive troubleshooting including failed sandbox replication, a call to walk through timeline, and a full worked RCA showing the exact interest-share formula and how the February data fix interacted with a later backdated Fee LPT to cause two consecutive months of incorrect payout.
current_status: Closed - resolved via data-fix correcting Interest Posted on the contract and related IPTs; classified as a data-fix issue, not a bug.

subject: Investor Fee Payout discrepancies in Production related to case no: 03800704
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Despite the earlier patch from case 03800704, a new fee-payout discrepancy occurred on full redemption of LAI-1110: the fee distribution matched neither the original nor the current investor share percentage.
issue_summary: Fee payout is calculated using each investor's original (fixed at investment) share percentage relative to total ACTIVE investor shares (not remaining investment amount), so as investors become inactive or partially redeem, the fee-share formula (Late_Fees_Paid = feeAmount * (investorShare/totalActiveShares) * (feeInvestorShare%)) produces results that don't track a share based on outstanding investment - confirmed as fundamental system design behaviour rather than a bug, since changing it would affect all Q2 customers.
case_fix: Q2 ultimately committed to a custom code solution: a bespoke class to distribute fees based on Remaining Investment Amount rather than original share, shared with the customer's CK team in December 2024 after being escalated from an initial 'enhancement, ETA April 2025' position when the customer pushed back that a year's wait was unacceptable and asked for an interim workaround.
case_discussion: Extended dispute (Apr-Dec 2024) including detailed worked fee-calculation examples from Q2, customer insistence that the behaviour was unacceptable for F2F's business model, repeated escalations (Stephanie Skinner) over multi-month silences, and Q2 eventually pivoting from 'enhancement in a future release' to building and delivering a custom-code fix.
current_status: Closed - resolved via a custom-built fee-distribution class calculating fee shares against Remaining Investment Amount; delivered to the customer's CK team for testing.

subject: LAI - 1259 : CL Contract Not Getting Closed after Pay Off
description: Backdated payoff of LAI-1259 in production produced two LPTs, one with payment mode 'Excess', with the current month's interest routing to Excess instead of clearing interest; the contract got stuck in 'Active - Marked for Closure' instead of closing.
issue_summary: Root cause traced to manual edits made directly to Charge records after their creation (dates and Principal Due/Original Amount changed on CHG-00015742/43/44/24), which produced the anomalous excess-LPT-alongside-payoff-LPT behaviour; Q2 reproduced the same behaviour in Pre-Prod by replicating the same manual charge edits, and flagged that the same pattern recurred on another loan (LAI-765) mid-case.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) applied a manual data fix per occurrence: for LAI-1259, zeroed the excess amount on the relevant LPT, corrected Interest Paid, marked the IPT paid, set loan status to Closed, and corrected Today's Payoff/contract Interest Paid; a near-identical fix was applied when the same issue recurred on LAI-765 (transaction date correction, zeroing excess, updating contract status to 'Closed Obligation Met' and clearing accrual/remaining fields). Q2 advised against making manual edits to Charge records after creation going forward.
case_discussion: Customer pressure over the loan needing to close by a committed date; the issue recurred on a second loan (LAI-765) while the first was still being investigated, requiring a second round of data-fix; root cause identified as customer-side manual charge edits rather than a product bug.
current_status: Closed - resolved via manual data fixes on both affected loans; guidance given to avoid manual edits to Charge records after creation.

subject: Getting an error while funding a Loan Application in Production Org related to case no. 03920451
description: Recurrence of case 03920451's funding error: funding application APP-00001356 in production threw the same FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION ('Please select whether the Address is a Current or Previous Address') from clcommon.AccountTrigger, not replicable in pre-production; this time the customer captured and attached full logs.
issue_summary: Root cause fully identified this time: the custom setting 'Copy Common Address To Standard Address' was set to false, so clcommon.AccountTriggerHandler.copyStandardObjectAddressToCommonAddress copies the Account's billing/shipping address into a new clcommon Address record on update; the borrower account ('Beaumaris Property Limited') had an existing linked Address record missing the required Current/Previous Address selection, which F2F's custom validation rule (Add_Either_Previous_or_Current_Address) then rejected.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) identified the incomplete Address record and confirmed that enabling the 'Copy Common Address To Standard Address' custom setting to true would stop the trigger from creating a new (incomplete) address during funding, with no other expected impact; recommended testing in sandbox first.
case_discussion: Q2 provided a full explanation of the AccountTrigger address-copy logic (absent from the original case 03920451) and pinpointed the specific incomplete Address record and setting causing the intermittent failure.
current_status: Closed - root cause identified (incomplete Address record plus a custom setting); customer to test enabling 'Copy Common Address To Standard Address' to prevent recurrence.

subject: Investor payout issue on LAI-1222
urgency: Medium – 3: There is an impact to your business, but your business continues to function
description: Interest payment LPT-000029513 (£1,787.50, transaction date 21/05/2024) on LAI-1222, paid out via job on 25/05/2024, did not include any payout or ILT records for investor Ian Hutchings (ILID-0000014603), who had held the investment for exactly one day (22/04-23/04).
issue_summary: When an IO is sold and immediately resold in quick succession (chained IO sales across consecutive days), the resulting short-lived IO in the chain accrued one day of interest but no Interest Posting Transaction (IPT) was generated for it before the sale, so its accrued interest was never paid out - confirmed reproducible via a detailed chained-sale replication scenario the customer provided.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) replicated the issue internally, confirmed it as a bug, escalated to Engineering, and released a patch (Loan 3.5054.233, Marketplace 3.5003.10 + dependent packages) in August 2024 to ensure IPTs are correctly generated for short-lived IOs in a chained-sale scenario.
case_discussion: Q2 initially struggled to replicate; customer provided a precise multi-step chained IO-sale replication procedure which Q2 confirmed reproduced the bug internally; patch delayed slightly past its 5-Aug ETA but delivered same day after a customer escalation.
current_status: Closed - resolved via product patch fixing IPT generation for short-lived IOs created through chained same-period IO sales.

subject: Lender Swap Patch - Borrower enters arrears
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: On LAI-1540, when a borrower catches up a missed interest payment after an IO sale mid-arrears, the payment should satisfy the oldest outstanding Interest Posting for all investors equally, but instead the exited (selling) investor gets prioritized and paid their full accrued interest (including interest not yet due), leaving the remaining investor underpaid.
issue_summary: Payment allocation logic pays out based on prioritizing the exited investor's total accrued interest rather than allocating strictly to the oldest outstanding Interest Posting Transaction shared across all investors, violating F2F's 'oldest arrears first' policy and disadvantaging remaining investors whenever an IO sale occurs while a loan is in arrears.
case_fix: Q2 replicated internally, initially deemed it a Design change (not patchable) in Sept 2024, then after escalation delivered a patch (Loan 4.4001.199 / Marketplace 4.4001.15 + dependents) around the 4.4 upgrade; however, the customer's post-upgrade testing (per detailed test notes from Md Sameer, July 2025) found the patch still failed the arrears scenario - the exited investor was still prioritized and remaining investors underpaid on backdated bills. As of case closure, Q2's product team (Amit Melwani) agreed to treat it as a proper enhancement (PDRFF-4184) with a new case to be raised to track delivery.
case_discussion: Extremely long-running case (Jun 2024-Aug 2025) spanning over a year: initial 'not patchable, design change' classification, later reconsidered and a patch delivered around the version 4.4 upgrade, then failed customer acceptance testing against two detailed scenarios (good-standing IO sale passed; bad-standing/arrears IO sale still failed), ending with Q2 committing to a genuine product enhancement (PDRFF-4184) rather than a further patch attempt.
current_status: Closed - patch delivered did not fully resolve the arrears scenario; issue escalated to a tracked product enhancement (PDRFF-4184) via a new case.

subject: Data Fix Steps for 03594592
description: Tracking case for applying the data-correction document received for case 03594592 (no interest payout on full redemption): the underlying patch fixed new contracts, but existing contracts still required manual data correction, which this case was opened to track.
issue_summary: Administrative/tracking case only - no new defect; existing (pre-patch) contracts affected by the 03594592 no-interest-payout-on-redemption issue needed the previously-provided data-fix document applied manually.
case_fix: Customer applied the data-correction steps from the attached document ('1989_DataFix') to the affected existing contracts.
case_discussion: Minimal discussion; opened purely to track and close out the manual remediation work stemming from case 03594592's patch.

subject: UPGRADE CASE - FOLK2FOLK - Q2 Version Upgrade (3.5 to 4.4)

subject: Solution for Optimising Testing process in Sandbox
description: Asked whether it's safe to speed up sandbox testing by marking all loans except a select few as invalid before doing large date-movement tests (e.g. Jan 2023 to Jul 2024), then reverting to the original date and revalidating all contracts afterward.
issue_summary: Needed confirmation that temporarily invalidating most sandbox contracts to isolate date-movement testing to a few loans would not cause long-term issues.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) confirmed the approach is fine with no expected long-term issues, since invalidated contracts are excluded from all managed-package job processing.
case_discussion: Simple clarification question, answered directly with no further back-and-forth.
