subject: Rescheduling Loan Error after Partial Redemption
description: Rescheduling a loan (e.g. LAI-987) after a partial redemption produces an incorrect repayment schedule: without 'Maintain Delinquency' the schedule includes all posted interest incorrectly, while with 'Maintain Delinquency' set to true, Principal appears incorrectly in multiple future months, making other schedule fields wrong.
issue_summary: Rescheduling logic mishandles the interaction between a prior partial redemption and the Maintain Delinquency flag, producing an incorrect preview/repayment schedule; reproducibility was inconsistent - confirmed replicable in lower orgs by the customer at one point, but Q2 repeatedly failed to reproduce it internally with the general steps given, and later customer re-tests (Nov 2024) also failed to reproduce it, including on version 4.4.
case_fix: No fix delivered; ultimately closed with sub-status 'Issue Not Resolved' after neither party could consistently reproduce the issue, with Q2 suggesting it may already be fixed in version 4.4 via other rescheduling-related patches.
case_discussion: Long-running case (Jul-Dec 2024) plagued by replication difficulty on both sides; multiple detailed replication step sets provided; a second occurrence reported on LAI-1145; case was reopened once after an earlier closure attempt when the customer said they hadn't finished testing; ultimately closed unresolved.
current_status: Closed as Issue Not Resolved - inconsistent/failed reproduction on both sides; possibly already addressed by unrelated 4.4 rescheduling patches.

subject: Incorrect Payout for LAI-1270
description: On LAI-1270, an investor whose IO (ILTID-0000308193) was sold on 15/09/2023 still received a payout of £231.11 on LPT-31508 nearly 10 months later, on 12/07/2024; a second similar instance was reported mid-case on another sold IO (ILTID-0000309417 / LPT-000031599, sold Oct 2023, paid out on a 15/07 redemption).
issue_summary: Recurrence of the sold-IO-continuing-to-accrue-and-pay-interest pattern from case 03824216 (and similar to case 04033854), occurring even on contracts with the latest patch installed, confirmed reproducible in the patched sandbox by the customer.
case_fix: Q2 (Utkarsh Saxena) confirmed the general sold-IO accrual issue was fixed in the 3.5 patch for new contracts, but that pre-existing affected contracts still needed a manual data fix (setting accrued interest to 0 for all sold investors); case closed after the customer was expected to apply this fix to the flagged contracts.
case_discussion: Extended troubleshooting (Jul-Oct 2024) including confirming reproducibility even with the latest patch, linking the pattern to related case 04033854, and repeated requests to confirm the manual data fix had been applied to affected contracts before closure.
current_status: Closed - root cause linked to known sold-IO interest-accrual issue; manual data fix (zeroing accrued interest for sold investors) applied to affected contracts.

subject: UPG 4.4 Set Password Redirection Link
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: After the 4.4 upgrade, setting a user's password via the CL Portal 'setPassword' remote action redirected to a malformed URL with the community prefix duplicated ('/investor/investor/apex/CommunitiesLanding' or '/borrower/borrower/apex/CommunitiesLanding'), producing a File Not Found page; manually removing one '/investor/' segment fixed it. Not reproducible in UAT (pre-4.4).
issue_summary: The 4.4 password-reset redirect logic doubled the community URL prefix when a community prefix was configured, breaking the post-password-set redirect for both Investor and Borrower portals.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) identified the double community-prefix bug in the redirect logic and delivered a fix so the redirect correctly includes the prefix only once.
case_discussion: Required detailed reproduction info (Visualforce page/component names, package version screenshots, recordings) and a screen-share call before Q2 could pin down and fix the double-prefix bug.
current_status: Closed - resolved via fix to the password-reset redirect logic removing the duplicated community prefix.

subject: UPG 4.4 Application Department is not being created via the portal
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: After upgrading to 4.4, applications created via the Guest Profile registration flow (using genesis.BorrowerAPI4.createApplication through a 'without sharing' portal API) succeeded in creating the Application record, but associated departments and tasks failed to generate; granting the Guest Profile read access to the Application object worked around it, but F2F was wary of that security exposure.
issue_summary: Task generation failed because the Guest Profile lacked read access to a custom field ('POA Applicable') on the Application object used as a criterion for generating a linked task ('Upload POA Certificate'); Q2 suspected version 4.4's product API may now enforce sharing/'WITH SECURITY ENFORCED' more strictly than 3.5, so Guest-Profile-created applications return zero records for such criteria checks without additional object access.
case_fix: No product-side fix; Q2 confirmed the underlying product team's official position that Guest-user flows should be limited to Account/Portal user creation only, and that enabling further object access for Application creation via Guest Profile carries security risk - if F2F chooses to proceed anyway, they must implement and own the necessary security configuration themselves.
case_discussion: Q2 could not reproduce the missing-department issue in their own DEV environment without any special Guest Profile access, suggesting an org-specific configuration difference; ultimately resolved via a policy/guidance answer rather than a technical fix.
current_status: Closed - Q2 advised against expanding Guest Profile access for Application creation due to security risk; no product fix provided, decision left to F2F.

subject: Rescheduling Error
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Backdating a reschedule on LAI-957 with Maintain Delinquency enabled included Principal in multiple months of the preview schedule, corrupting other schedule columns - similar symptom to case 04016708 but without any prior partial redemption on this loan; the loan was fully redeemed before the issue could be investigated further.
issue_summary: Same family of rescheduling/Maintain-Delinquency schedule-preview bug as case 04016708, but occurring without a partial redemption precondition, suggesting a broader triggering condition than initially thought; could not be investigated further once the loan redeemed and closed.
case_fix: No fix delivered; case closed because the affected contract had since closed and no other reproducible instance in production or sandbox was available to investigate against.

subject: UPG 4.4 Payout Issue upon Full Redemption of Delinquent Loan followed by IO Sale and Fee Payout
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: In 4.4 sandbox testing (LAI-00001574/1575): a 3-term contract had one IO sold 10 days in, went delinquent past the 1st due date and was rescheduled to a higher rate, then a fee-only LPT was paid 20 days past due; the fee payout job also accrued an extra day of interest on the already-sold IO, so when the loan was paid off at the 2nd due date, total payout (sum of ILTs) didn't match the LPT: Interest overpaid by £3.34 and Fee underpaid by £111.12 relative to the LPT amounts.
issue_summary: Running the payout job for a fee-only LPT on a delinquent loan with a previously sold IO incorrectly accrued one extra day of interest on the sold IO, causing interest to be overpaid and fee amounts to be misallocated versus the LPT totals; confirmed reproducible internally by Q2, a genuine bug in the 4.4 line.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) released a patch (Loan 4.4001.104, Marketplace 4.4001.1 + dependent packages including CL Common 4.4000.7 or the customer's already-installed 4.4000.10) in late August 2024 to correct the extra-day interest accrual during fee-only payout on delinquent, previously-sold-IO contracts.
case_discussion: Customer provided detailed replication steps and screenshots; Q2 confirmed reproducibility internally fairly quickly and delivered the patch within about a month, with an upgrade-timeline escalation from Amelia Bailey pushing for an ETA; a version-compatibility question about CL Common was resolved by confirming the customer's already-higher-installed version was fine to use.
current_status: Closed - resolved via product patch (Loan 4.4001.104/Marketplace 4.4001.1) fixing extra-day interest accrual in the delinquent+sold-IO+fee-payout scenario.

subject: UPG 4.4 Payout Issue on delinquent loan after IOs Sale
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: In 4.4 sandbox testing (LAI-00001576): a delinquent loan had one IO sold to two new investors (A sold simultaneously to B and C) partway through, then two more IOs sold later; when the first month's interest LPT was cleared, payout incorrectly went to the newly-created IOs from the second month's sales rather than only the IOs that existed since contract creation (as no IO sales had occurred in month one) - interest underpaid by £72.14 relative to the LPT (£750.00 LPT vs £677.86 in ILTs).
issue_summary: When an IO is sold simultaneously to two buyers, no Interest Posting Transaction is generated for the original (sold) investor and its 'Income to be Collected' flag incorrectly remains false, so that investor's rightful share of interest is never allocated and payout ends up misdirected to the wrong IOs; confirmed as a genuine 4.4-line bug after internal replication.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) released a patch (Loan 4.4001.135, Marketplace 4.4001.10 + dependent packages including CL Common 4.4000.19) on 7 October 2024 to correctly generate the Interest Posting Transaction and set the Income to be Collected flag when an IO is sold to multiple simultaneous buyers.
case_discussion: Detailed customer-provided replication steps and financial analysis; Q2 successfully replicated internally in about two weeks and characterized the exact defect (missing IPT and flag on simultaneous dual-buyer IO sale) before committing to and delivering the October patch, with escalation pressure from Amelia Bailey over ETA given the upgrade timeline.
current_status: Closed - resolved via product patch fixing IPT generation and Income-to-be-Collected flag on simultaneous multi-buyer IO sales.

subject: UPG 4.4 Attempt to de-reference a null object from CL Integration Framework
description: After the 4.4 upgrade, making a callout through CL Integration Framework to F2F's custom third-party integration (Acuris, via a custom AcurisPostPersonAdapter class) failed with 'Attempt to de-reference a null object' before the adapter's generateRequestBody method executed; not reproducible in the pre-upgrade (3.5/UAT) org.
issue_summary: Root cause traced to changes in Integration Framework's adapter validation flow in 4.4: F2F's custom adapter performed parameter validation inside generateRequestBody() (rather than the framework's dedicated validateRequestParameters() method), and a required value (monitorRecordId/worklistId, tied to changes in the PostPerson Adapter API and Integration API Record configuration) was no longer being initialized before validation ran, causing the null dereference; JIRA PDRFF-3397 was raised.
case_fix: Q2 (Jorge Maceda, with PS/Engineering) instructed the customer to move parameter validation out of generateRequestBody() into the framework's validateRequestParameters() override, update the Integration API Record's request mapping (using 'worklistId' as a path parameter) and endpoint value, and update the AcurisPostPersonAdapter's sendRequest() method accordingly; customer applied the changes and confirmed resolution.
case_discussion: Extended multi-week log-comparison investigation (Aug-Sep 2024) between the upgraded and non-upgraded orgs, including a detour into an unrelated Salesforce storage-limit-exceeded error, several calls, and detailed line-by-line code walkthroughs of the custom adapter and controller classes before the framework-level validation-flow change was pinpointed as the cause.
current_status: Closed - resolved by moving custom adapter validation into validateRequestParameters() and updating Integration API Record configuration per Q2's guidance.

subject: UPG 4.4 Investor Payout Discrepancy Post Payoff on Partially Redeemed Loan
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: In 4.4 sandbox testing (LAI-00001578/1579): after a partial redemption with per-investor priority set (so some investors got fully repaid first) followed by removal of that priority and a later full payoff, the final payoff LPT's principal distribution was incoherent - LPT-000003480 principal of £95,800.00 vs. ILT sum of £69,486.93 (difference £26,313.07); some IOs went inactive despite not having received their full principal.
issue_summary: The system always calculates principal/fee payout using each investor's ORIGINAL fixed investment share percentage rather than their current outstanding share; when temporary investor payout priorities are set (to fully repay some investors first) and later removed, subsequent payouts to the remaining investors are miscalculated against original shares that no longer reflect reality, since the prioritized investors already received their money - confirmed as a bug reproducible internally and tied to the same original-share-based design flaw seen in cases 03816738/03942142/03613074.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) confirmed this required a genuine design change - calculating payout based on current/remaining investment share (remaining investment amount over remaining contract principal) instead of original share - and committed the fix to a New Design item, prioritized given the upgrade-timeline pressure; ultimately marked resolved in a later 4.4 version.
case_discussion: Extensive multi-month case (Aug-Oct 2024) with detailed replication steps (5 investors, priority-based partial payoff followed by unprioritized full payoff), escalations from Amelia Bailey citing upgrade-schedule risk, confirmation the underlying design flaw predates 4.4 (same class of issue as older case 03613074), and eventual resolution folded into a newer 4.4 patch version.
current_status: Closed - resolved in a later 4.4 version via a design change calculating payout against current/remaining investment share instead of original share.

subject: Error::API_EXCEPTION : Insert failed - Error while disbursement
description: Disbursing loan application APP-1408 via F2FDisburseLoan (custom class calling peer.FundLoanApplicationCtrl.fundLoanApplication) threw 'API_EXCEPTION: Insert failed... Attempt to de-reference a null object' at line 202 during the batch, blocking a same-day disbursal deadline.
issue_summary: F2F's custom Fee class (F2FFeeHandler) overrides the product's ComputeFee method, which returns a Decimal; when the loan application had no associated Collection Fee, the override returned null instead of zero, and the product API's rounding logic threw a null-dereference error trying to round that null value.
case_fix: The customer (Supriyo/Anup) identified the root cause themselves after Q2 pointed to the custom Fee class validation, and fixed it by updating F2FFeeHandler's ComputeFee override to return zero instead of null when no Collection Fee exists; tested successfully in a lower sandbox and applied in time for the disbursal deadline.
case_discussion: Same-day urgent turnaround given a disbursal deadline; Q2 (Shalini Panjavarnam) helped isolate the issue to the custom Fee class quickly via a revert test, after which the customer completed the actual code fix themselves.
current_status: Closed - resolved by customer fixing F2FFeeHandler to return zero instead of null for a missing Collection Fee.

subject: Daily Jobs got Stuck in 'Processing' Status on 24th August 2024
description: On 24 August 2024, the daily job loan.LoanBlockCodeExpiryProcessingDynamicJob got stuck in 'Processing' status, halting all subsequent chained daily jobs for that day; the issue did not recur from the 25th onward, and the cause was unclear.
issue_summary: A single dynamic job (ID 707N100000STsAW) hung in the processing stage without reaching its finish method and without throwing an error, for reasons that could not be determined from available logs; Salesforce's own investigation found no performance degradation around the job's run time and speculated it might be due to corrupt record data, but could not confirm since it was a one-off, unreproduced occurrence.
case_fix: No fix identified; Q2 (Bhanupriya Sharma) escalated to Salesforce support, who reviewed server logs and reported no explainable cause beyond a possible one-off data issue; case closed on the customer's agreement given the issue hadn't recurred.
case_discussion: Q2 raised a case directly with Salesforce for backend log review; the investigation concluded inconclusively, with a note that recurring instances would be needed to properly diagnose the root cause.
current_status: Closed - root cause undetermined (single non-recurring occurrence); Salesforce found no clear explanation beyond possible corrupt record data.

subject: UPG 4.4 Payout Issue after an IO is sold to more than one IOs
description: After upgrading to 4.4 and installing the 04033854 patch, testing an IO sold simultaneously to two new investors (with further full/partial resales of the resulting IOs) found that on the next due date, payout was short by exactly the amount owed on the originally dual-sold IO (LAI-00001665/1664).
issue_summary: Same underlying defect as case 04036422 - selling an IO to two investors at once fails to generate the correct Interest Posting Transaction/flag for the original investor, causing an underpayment.
case_fix: No separate fix; Q2 (Deeptha S) identified this as a duplicate of case 04036422 and had the customer track the fix (ETA 7 October patch) under that case instead.
case_discussion: Initial confusion over sandbox org/contract IDs before Q2 confirmed the described behaviour matched 04036422's already-diagnosed dual-buyer IO sale bug.
current_status: Closed as duplicate of case 04036422; resolved via that case's patch (Loan 4.4001.135).

subject: UPG 4.4 "Interest Only Period should be less than the contract term" error on backdated reschedule
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: After the 4.4 upgrade plus the 04033854 patch, manually rescheduling a delinquent loan (LAI-00001666) to a higher rate with a backdated transaction date threw 'Interest Only Period should be less than the contract term' at save time despite the preview looking correct and the Interest Only Period genuinely being less than the reschedule term.
issue_summary: A validation bug in the 4.4-line reschedule logic incorrectly rejected valid backdated reschedules where Interest Only Period was less than the reschedule term; a first patch (4.4001.139) fixing the reported scenario introduced a new regression where reschedule transactions dated equal to the pre-bill-days boundary (i.e., transaction date = system date) generated an incorrect repayment schedule.
case_fix: Q2 (Sagar Kanvihalli Seetharama / Rohit Datta) delivered patch 4.4001.139 (Oct 2024) fixing the original validation error, then a follow-up patch 4.4001.157 (18 Nov 2024) fixing the newly discovered pre-bill-days-boundary regression; customer given an interim workaround (create the backdated payment with a transaction date less than the pre-bill-days period) while the second fix was pending.
case_discussion: Long case (Sep-Dec 2024) with heavy upgrade-schedule pressure from Amelia Bailey pushing for ETAs given a planned December production upgrade; customer explicitly paused patch installation after impact analysis showed the first patch's regression could affect a large percentage of loans, until the follow-up fix was delivered.
current_status: Closed - resolved via two sequential patches (4.4001.139 then 4.4001.157) addressing the original validation bug and a regression it introduced.

subject: Priority 0 in Sold IOs
description: A sold IO (ILID-0000008190) received a £475.00 payout on LPT-000034428 nearly a year after being sold, causing other active investors to miss out on their interest payment; investigation showed the payout job assigned the sold IO Priority 0 starting from 02/09/2024, the date F2F's own production patches (the 3.5054.223 Loan/Marketplace patch set from earlier cases) were installed.
issue_summary: Following the installed patches, the payout job's design now prioritizes sold investors whenever there is a residual mismatch between Interest Remaining and Interest Amount Paid on the IO, paying them the full amount to zero out that mismatch - even though the customer's own history tracking showed the IO had no residual value in the Interest Posted field at the time of payout, contradicting Q2's initial explanation. A separate, similar payout issue was identified on a different loan (LAI-1048) and spun off as its own matter.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) provided a data-fix procedure: reverse the LPT and its payout, correct the sold investor's Interest Remaining to match Interest Amount Paid, zero out its accrued interest, apply this to all sold investors on the contract, then create a new payoff LPT and rerun the investor payout job.
case_discussion: Customer pushed back on Q2's first explanation (residual Interest Posted value) with history-tracking evidence showing no such residual existed, prompting further investigation; a related issue on LAI-1048 was explicitly separated out into a new case rather than conflated with this one.
current_status: Closed - resolved via manual data-fix reversing and recreating the payoff LPT with corrected investor interest values; related LAI-1048 issue tracked separately.

subject: Investor Payout Discrepancy on LAI - 766
description: LPT-000034434 on LAI-766 (transaction date 17/09/2024, fully towards interest) paid out £617.42 across investors versus an LPT amount of only £425.82 - payout exceeding the actual transaction amount.
issue_summary: Contract-level and investor-level Interest Posted amounts had drifted out of sync (contract £1,338.48 vs. total investor-side £1,146.88 at review time, and a similarly mismatched figure at the time of the LPT payout itself), so the payout formula (LPT amount × investor-share-of-contract-interest) produced an inflated result; root cause attributed to a combination of prior bugs and investor interest posting not having been enabled from the investor's actual start date.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) provided a worked reconciliation and proposed the customer either reverse the affected payment and correct the investor-side Interest Posted to align with the contract, or amend the currently posted amounts directly, plus ensure investor accrued interest matches contract accrued interest going forward.
case_discussion: Detailed RCA walking through specific ILID interest-posted figures at different points in time to demonstrate the drift between contract- and investor-level interest; resolved via a proposed reconciliation approach rather than a code patch.
current_status: Closed - resolved via realigning investor-side and contract-side Interest Posted amounts per Q2's reconciliation guidance.

subject: LAI - 1048 Payout issue
description: Follow-up on LAI-1048 (previously flagged in case 04086274): the total payout amount for a recent payment was correct in aggregate, but most active investors received less than expected because sold investors on the loan were paid out first.
issue_summary: Confirmed as the same sold-investor-payout-prioritization behaviour seen in cases 04086274/03824216 - the system now prioritizes paying sold investors in full before active investors, which can leave active investors underpaid relative to their posted interest if the sold/active split of total posted interest isn't perfectly balanced.
case_fix: No fix; Q2 (Rohit Datta) explained this is intended current system behaviour (sold investors compensated first since they're no longer part of the investment), and that totals will reconcile correctly only if sold- and active-side posted interest sums are already accurate.
case_discussion: Direct explanatory response tying the issue back to the recently changed sold-investor-priority payout design discussed across several other cases (04086274, 03824216, 03782238).
current_status: Closed - explained as expected sold-investor-priority payout behaviour; no fix delivered.

subject: Bill generated of Amount zero after rescheduling a Loan with maintain delinquency as true
description: On LAI-1387, a £1,879.17 bill was generated 11 days before the due date; the loan was then rescheduled to a higher rate the next day with a backdated transaction date and Maintain Delinquency = true, after which the next billing job run generated a new bill of £0 instead of the expected higher amount. With Maintain Delinquency = false, the next bill generated correctly. Also observed on LAI-00000844, LAI-00000873, and LAI-00001546.
issue_summary: Rescheduling with Maintain Delinquency enabled after a bill has already been generated for the current cycle produces a follow-on £0 bill instead of a corrected higher-amount bill; Q2's own review of production found LAI-1387 actually had two bills generated (one £0, PCN-0000016065, and a correct one for £5,857.50, PCN-0000016103), suggesting the £0 bill may be superseded rather than final.
case_fix: No definitive fix delivered within this case; it was closed automatically after 2+ weeks of no customer response (customer was mid-way through replicating in UAT), and a new case (04123634) was opened to continue the investigation.
case_discussion: Q2 requested production and UAT access and ran its own tests, finding a second, correct bill alongside the reported £0 one; case auto-closed per Q2's inactivity policy before the customer could complete UAT replication, and was recreated as case 04123634 to continue.
current_status: Closed (auto-closed due to inactivity) - investigation continued under new case 04123634; Q2's review suggested the £0 bill may be superseded by a correct follow-up bill.

subject: 0.063p to excess on Management Fee in Production related to case Id 03727405
description: Follow-up to case 03727405: the Management Fee charge CHG-00007165 on LAI-00000938 was split across two LPTs for March 2023 (£250 and £0.00) and then April's clearing LPT paid £249.99 towards the charge instead of the two months cleanly totalling £250 via a single LPT, leaving a fraction of a penny mismatched; a manual data fix was applied. A previously provided code change to F2F's custom F2FUpdatePeriodicFeeBatch (line 117) did not fully resolve it, and the issue was not reproducible in the Dev sandbox.
issue_summary: A small residual rounding/allocation discrepancy (fractions of a penny) in custom fee-batch logic causes Management Fee charges to be split unevenly across LPTs in some production cases, not reliably reproducible outside production.
case_fix: No definitive fix delivered within the case; Q2 (Rohit Datta) requested logs from a live recurrence (via reversing and re-running an affected LPT) to analyze further, and asked whether the issue appeared in the new 4.4 version; customer confirmed it does NOT occur in 4.4 and is not reproducible in lower sandboxes, and continued applying manual data fixes as instances arose.
case_discussion: Extended troubleshooting (Oct-Dec 2024) hampered by non-reproducibility outside production; confirmed the issue does not affect the 4.4 version, somewhat reducing urgency since F2F was migrating.
current_status: Closed - unresolved as a root-cause code fix; mitigated by manual data fixes; confirmed not present in version 4.4.

subject: Incorrect interest posting for a 31-day month following a missed payment from the previous month
description: With a 13-day delinquency grace period intended to produce 14 days of lower-rate interest followed by 16 days of higher-rate interest after a missed payment and reschedule, some loans (LAI-1048, LAI-1430) instead accrued 13 days at the lower rate and 17 at the higher rate when the missed payment fell in a 31-day month; the pattern did not occur after a 30-day month (e.g. LAI-1148).
issue_summary: The 'Months and Days' (30/360) time counting method skips the 31st day for interest accrual purposes but still counts it toward days-past-due/delinquency calculations, so the reschedule trigger fires one day earlier relative to interest-day counting than F2F's intended 14/16-day split, whenever the missed due date falls just after a 31-day month; confirmed by Q2 as standard product behaviour (time counting method governs only interest calculation, not due-date/delinquency calculation) rather than a bug.
case_fix: No fix; Q2 (Rachita Arora) confirmed this is expected behaviour across all time counting methods (also verified for Actual Days/366) and recommended the customer submit it as a product enhancement/idea via the Customer Portal Ideas Page, providing instructions on how to do so.
case_discussion: Detailed comparative analysis across time counting methods; customer accepted this is a business-requirement gap rather than a defect and was guided toward submitting a formal enhancement idea instead of pursuing further troubleshooting.
current_status: Closed - confirmed as expected product behaviour, not a bug; customer directed to submit a product enhancement idea via the Customer Portal.

subject: IO Sale Issue: Principal Amount paid Not Populating and Interest Not Posted Post-Sale
description: Two IO-sale scenarios re-tested in pre-production (to isolate whether caused by a recent patch): (1) on a partial IO sale, the 'Principal Paid' column didn't reflect the £12,500 paid at time of sale; (2) the current month's interest accrued on the original IO was copied to the new IO for the remaining amount, and when interest was later paid out it applied to the new IO which hadn't actually accrued it. Confirmed consistent in pre-prod (LAI-00001606, LAI-00001406 across two orgs, both on Loan Servicing 3.5054.223).
issue_summary: Potential pre-existing IO-sale defects (Principal Paid not populating on partial sale; interest misattributed to the new post-sale IO) that the customer wanted distinguished from a regression introduced by a recently installed patch.
case_fix: Not resolved within this case; Q2 (Jesus Diaz) asked several clarifying questions (patch install date, whether reproducible before the patch, production vs UAT scope, sandbox version history) that went unanswered long enough for the case to auto-close; a new case was requested to continue investigation.
current_status: Closed (auto-closed due to inactivity) - clarifying questions on patch timing/scope unanswered; customer asked to open a new case to continue.

subject: Excess LPT On Loan Payoff - Payout Allocation across capital/interest/fees looks wrong
description: On some loan payoffs (LPT-000034432 of LAI-00000698, LPT-000034430 of LAI-00000699), the system generates an additional 'Excess' payment-mode LPT alongside the main payoff LPT, and the sum of ILT principal amounts doesn't match the LPT principal because ILTs attach to only one of the two LPTs, not split correctly across both.
issue_summary: Intermittent generation of a spurious Excess LPT during certain loan payoffs, with ILT allocation not properly split/matched across the resulting two LPTs - occurring only on a subset of contracts with no clear replication steps identified.
case_fix: No fix delivered within the case; Q2 (Rohit Datta) asked for a full list of affected contracts and confirmation of whether the issue occurs in 4.4, but the case was auto-closed once before due to no update, then reopened; case ultimately closed again with the affected-contracts list still being compiled.
case_discussion: Q2 maintained that a payoff should always process as a single LPT and requested reproducible steps and a full impacted-contract list; customer could only confirm it was intermittent and contract-specific without a clear trigger; access/LMA renewal delays also slowed investigation.
current_status: Closed - root cause not resolved; affected-contracts list requested but investigation did not reach a fix before closure.

subject: Priority 0 in Sold IOs
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Following the 02/09/2024 patch (also implicated in case 04086274), sold IOs are now assigned payout priority 0. On LAI-1243, when a waived-type LPT (LPT-000036702) and a regular LPT (LPT-000036703) both paid out on 14/11/2024, the waived LPT first paid the sold IO (ILID-0000006467) its full £179.87 outstanding interest, leaving it with zero interest posted; when the subsequent regular LPT ran, the sold IO received nothing (since it had none left to pay), producing cascading incorrect payouts to all IOs, contrary to F2F's requirement that sold IOs not be automatically prioritized.
issue_summary: A system behaviour change from the recent patch now always pays sold/exited investors first and in full, rather than distributing pro-rata across active and sold IOs alike - directly conflicting with F2F's business requirement and causing repeated payout miscalculations whenever multiple LPTs (e.g. a waived one followed by a regular one) process on the same day for a contract with a sold IO.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) confirmed the sold-investor-priority behaviour is the current intended product design post-patch, not a bug that can simply be reverted; committed to a broader design change (already implemented in version 4.6, parameterized to coexist with the existing behaviour) that allocates borrower payments to the oldest outstanding IPTs matching the loan contract's own IPT dates, and said they would check whether this could be backported/patched to 4.4. The case was ultimately closed by merging into case 04156782 covering the same underlying issue.
case_discussion: Long-running case (Nov 2024-Mar 2025) reiterating the same sold-investor-priority root cause as 04086274/04095016, with Q2 committing to a genuine parameterized redesign (targeting oldest-IPT-first allocation) already live in 4.6, uncertain whether backportable to 4.4; ultimately consolidated with case 04156782 rather than closed independently.
current_status: Closed - merged into case 04156782 tracking the same sold-IO-priority payout redesign; a 4.6 fix exists, 4.4 backport uncertain at time of closure.

subject: IO Sale Issue: Principal Amount paid Not Populating and Interest Not Posted Post-Sale
description: Re-raised duplicate of case 04124361 (same description, same IOs/LAIs: ILID-0000005279/5281 of LAI-00001606, and ILID-0000008534 of LAI-00001406) after that case auto-closed for inactivity - partial IO sale not reflecting Principal Paid, and interest misapplied to the new post-sale IO.
issue_summary: Same potential IO-sale defects as case 04124361, needing verification against the recently installed patch.
case_fix: Q2 (Shalini Panjavarnam) replicated a partial-IO-sale scenario end-to-end in the customer's own sandbox org (00DPu000003r3kP) and found Principal Paid populated correctly and interest posted/paid as expected, contradicting the reported issue; after repeated unanswered follow-up requests for the org access and clarification needed to reproduce the customer's exact scenario, the case was closed on the assumption the issue was not actually occurring.
case_discussion: Q2 provided a documented successful replication with screenshot evidence showing correct behaviour in the customer's own sandbox, but could not get further engagement from the customer to reconcile this with the originally reported discrepancy.
current_status: Closed - Q2's own replication in the customer's sandbox showed correct behaviour; closed after no further customer response.

subject: UPG - Payout Behaviour in CL Loan Version 3.5054.223 and 4.4
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Formal consolidation/escalation of the sold-IO-payout-priority issue (first introduced by the 3.5054.223 patch for case 04086274 on 2 Sept 2024, carried into 4.4): detailed multi-IO-sale-chain replication steps showed incorrect investor payout calculation once a loan with several chained IO sales went delinquent, was rescheduled, and had only partial dues cleared - urgent given F2F's 4.4 upgrade deadline and impending team unavailability over the holidays.
issue_summary: The sold-investor-payout-priority behaviour (from case 04086274/04133925) produces incorrect payouts specifically when an LPT's transaction date is on or before the IO's sale date: the sold investor is always credited the full posted amount regardless of whether that reflects a same-date or backdated payment relative to the sale, and this 'over-credit' pattern re-emerges any time prioritization logic isn't properly accounted for.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) determined a full architectural fix (not a simple patch rollback) was needed and committed engineering resources given the upgrade deadline; F2F pushed for a rollback of the original patch as a 'Plan B' if the fix wasn't ready in time; Q2 ultimately delivered a comprehensive patch (Loan 4.4001.194, Marketplace 4.4001.13 + dependent packages including CL Common 4.4000.24) in April 2025 addressing the payout allocation logic across both scenarios described in the RCA.
case_discussion: High-stakes case spanning Dec 2024-May 2025 with F2F (Amelia Bailey) explicitly threatening to roll back the original patch and delay their 4.4 upgrade if a proper fix wasn't forthcoming; Q2 provided a detailed two-scenario RCA (same-date vs backdated LPT relative to sale date) before committing to and delivering the architectural fix months later.
current_status: Closed - resolved via comprehensive patch (Loan 4.4001.194/Marketplace 4.4001.13) addressing sold-IO payout prioritization across both root-cause scenarios.

subject: Discrepancies in Investor Payout Calculations in CL Loan v3.5054.223
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Since the 3.5054.223 patch (2 Sept 2024), recurring small (penny-level) investor payout discrepancies appeared across multiple loans (LAI-1638, LAI-1351, LAI-1138, LAI-1134, LAI-811, LAI-1503, LAI-1670, and more): interest posted vs. payment approval amounts drift by a penny or more in ways that don't follow the expected 3-month rounding-accumulation pattern, sometimes resolving itself, sometimes compounding, occasionally overpaying investors by several pence (a client-money-breach concern if it were an underpayment instead).
issue_summary: A rounding/carry-forward defect, most clearly tied to sold investors: when an IO is sold, accumulated sub-penny rounding differences are not correctly carried forward to the new IO, causing small but real discrepancies between what's posted and what's paid out; the pattern was intermittent, hard to reproduce on demand, and initially dismissed by Q2 as 'not a bug' (a rounding artifact) before being accepted as reproducible and fixable.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta / Amit Melwani) eventually reproduced the issue internally, identified the specific defect (rounding not carried forward on sold investors), and delivered a patch (Loan 4.4001.232, Marketplace 4.4001.15 + dependent packages including CL Common 4.4000.37) in October 2025; UAT and Preprod testing followed, with the patch confirmed live and issue-free as of Feb 2026 (though the customer noted such scenarios are rare so real-world confirmation would take time).
case_discussion: Extremely long-running case (Jan 2025-Oct 2025) with Md Sameer providing many detailed real-world examples across numerous loans over many months, initial Q2 skepticism that this was a bug at all ('not a significant difference... does not appear to be a bug'), an explicit flag that undetected underpayments would constitute a client money breach, and eventual internal replication tied specifically to the sold-investor rounding carry-forward gap; testing then proceeded through multiple environments (UAT, Preprod) before going live.
current_status: Closed - resolved via patch (Loan 4.4001.232) fixing rounding carry-forward for sold investors; live in production as of Feb 2026 with no reported recurrences at closure, though customer to report any future instances given the scenario's rarity.

subject: MAF Charge Allocation Issue
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Three contracts (LAI-1036, 938, 715), and later others (LAI-909, 1134, etc.), have had a recurring near-two-year-old pattern since April/May 2023 where each month's Management/Admin Fee (MAF) payment clears all but exactly £0.01 of the charge, leaving a persistent 1p shortfall that rolls forward every month regardless of attempts (e.g. manually waiving the 1p) to break the cycle; a related 0.07p Excess had also accumulated on one loan.
issue_summary: A sub-penny rounding/allocation defect in fee/charge clearing causes a persistent 1p (or similar tiny) shortfall to perpetually roll forward on affected MAF charges; root cause eventually tied (per case 04189822's related investigation) to decimal/rounding handling in IPT posting and charge allocation, with at least one instance (LAI-909) traced to an LPT reversal creating a 1-cent-shifted replacement IPT that threw off subsequent MAF allocations.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta / Amit Melwani) eventually replicated the RCA and applied manual data fixes on the specific affected contracts (confirmed complete on LAI-938, with LAI-909 found to have no outstanding issue); a systemic patch was not delivered under this case specifically, with the broader rounding root cause tracked via the related case 04189822.
case_discussion: Very long-running case (Feb-Sep 2025) that started with Q2 unable to find the referenced contracts in the wrong sandbox org, repeated requests for reproducible steps/logs on a bug that couldn't be replicated in lower environments, customer providing many additional real-world examples over months, and eventual RCA replication leading to targeted data fixes rather than a blanket code patch.
current_status: Closed - resolved via manual data fixes on specific affected contracts (e.g. LAI-938); broader systemic rounding root cause tracked under related case 04189822.

subject: Excess LPT On Loan Payoff - Payout Allocation across capital/interest/fees looks wrong
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue

current_status: Closed - issue not observed since the production upgrade to version 4.4; no specific patch was needed or delivered.

subject: Redemption Payout Exceeds Matched Amount LAI 768 (Compliance)
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Flagged as a regulatory/compliance concern: LAI-768 redeemed on 28/02/2025 (related to the Excess-LPT issue in case 04217018); F2F matched £2,435 of interest and investor-attributed fee-interest at redemption, but the system generated a payout of £2,485 - a £50 overpayment that would have breached client-money regulations had it not been caught by manual validation before disbursement.
issue_summary: Root cause traced to a specific LPT (LPT-000037413) that had been cleared and then, when an attempt was made to reverse it, was instead erroneously REJECTED with its Cleared flag manually set back to false - meaning a prior £50 payment was never properly reversed/refunded in the system's records, so at final settlement the full £2,020 interest (including the un-reversed £50) was disbursed to the investor against a contract that should only have owed £1,970.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) identified this as a user/process data error (incorrect LPT rejection instead of proper reversal) rather than a system compliance bug, and emphasized that LPTs must be reversed correctly (not rejected) after being cleared to avoid this in future.
case_discussion: Q2 traced the exact transaction history showing the LPT's cleared-flag was manually reset rather than going through a proper reversal, clarifying that this was an operational/process error on the customer side rather than a product defect.
current_status: Closed - root cause identified as an incorrect manual LPT rejection instead of a proper reversal; classified as user/process error, not a system bug; guidance given on correct LPT reversal procedure.

subject: Interest Payout Exceeds Matched Amount - LAI 736 (Compliance)

description: Flagged as a regulatory/compliance concern: on delinquent loan LAI-736, a borrower payment of £4,373.99 matched on 4 March was followed by incorrect payment approvals that overpaid each investor by about 0.1666%, for a total payout of £5,102.98 - £728.98 more than was actually matched; caught by manual validation before disbursement. A second, smaller instance (LPT-000006247, paid £1,041.66 instead of £833.34) was also found on the same contract.

current_status: Closed - correction values provided for both overpaid LPTs; classified as a manual-payment data issue, not a systemic bug; closed due to inactivity before customer confirmed applying the fix.

subject: Investor Swaps - Previously Sold IOs
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Selling an IO that had itself previously been partially sold does not work cleanly for estate/succession transfers (e.g. a deceased joint investor's share moving to the surviving party, or to a will beneficiary). Two attempted methods both failed in practice: depositing the remaining investment amount and selling at price-per-share=1 left a stray small residual active IO; calculating price-per-share precisely to sell the full original amount hit an 'insufficient funds' error requiring the customer to temporarily deposit and then withdraw fabricated funds to force the transaction through.
issue_summary: The IO sale mechanism requires the selling account's available balance to match the full amount being 'sold' even when only the remaining (already-reduced-by-prior-partial-sale) investment amount is actually being transferred, forcing workarounds that either leave incorrect residual IOs or require temporarily falsifying account balances - both problematic for accurate financial reconciliation and future Investor Portal transparency.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) tested the insufficient-funds scenario in version 4.4 and confirmed it has already been resolved there (fix originally made for a different customer hitting the same issue in an earlier version); the residual-IO issue from the price-per-share=1 method was acknowledged by the customer as user error from not calculating price-per-share correctly rather than a product defect.
case_discussion: Customer provided two real production examples with full transaction detail; extensive manual effort was needed to calculate correct balances for the data correction; case closure was pending customer's own 4.4 testing to confirm the insufficient-funds problem was indeed fixed.
current_status: Closed - insufficient-funds workaround issue confirmed resolved in version 4.4; residual-IO issue attributed to user error in the price-per-share calculation, not a product defect.

subject: Partial Redemption Payout - Investor Prioritisation Failure (Compliance)
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Two loans redeemed the same day: LAI-1080 had 55 of its 64 active investors marked prioritized for a partial redemption payout, but the system paid principal to ALL 64 active investors, spreading the capital meant for 55 across all 64 and producing wrong amounts for everyone; LAI-1081 (15 of what should have been 14 prioritized, a human data-entry error) processed correctly despite the wrong prioritization count, confirming the defect was specific to LAI-1080's scenario, not prioritization generally. Caught before the payout file was finalized, avoiding a compliance breach; time pressure was acute since the next day's accrual job would compound the error if not fixed immediately.
issue_summary: The IO-sale/prioritization framework lacked the necessary underlying fields to correctly restrict payout distribution to only the prioritized subset of investors when the vast majority (55 of 64) were prioritized, causing the payout job to fall back to distributing across all active investors instead.
case_fix: Q2 (Vishal Lakkammanavar / Rohit Datta) reproduced the issue and provided a temporary workaround (reverse the loan payment and investor payout, reset IO priorities, reprocess) tested in pre-production same-day given the urgency; a lasting fix required new product fields as part of the IO Sale functionality, delivered as part of version 4.7 (December 2024) - to be adopted with F2F's next upgrade rather than backported.
case_discussion: Extremely time-critical same-day incident response (reproduced and a workaround attempted within hours of the report) given the risk of compounding the error in the next accrual run; longer-term resolution required a proper product enhancement (new IO Sale fields in 4.7) rather than a quick patch, with the case formally closed months later after a review call agreeing to treat 4.7 adoption as the resolution path.
current_status: Closed - temporary workaround applied same-day to correct the immediate payout; permanent fix (new IO Sale fields) delivered in version 4.7, to be adopted at F2F's next upgrade.

subject: DML Limit Error
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Sending manual communication emails to more than 150 selected investors at once threw 'Too many DML statements: 151' (LIMIT_EXCEEDED) post-upgrade; debug logs showed the underlying trigger inserts one notify_fw__Notification_Event__e platform event per task individually rather than in a single bulk DML, hitting Salesforce's per-transaction DML statement limit.
issue_summary: A managed-package trigger on the Task object publishes Notification Event platform events one row at a time instead of bulkifying the insert, so any bulk email send exceeding ~150 recipients (150 DML statements) fails outright, forcing a fallback to manual, smaller-batch sending.
case_fix: Q2 raised JIRA PDRFF-3843 with high priority for the product team to properly bulkify the event-publishing trigger; while awaiting a product fix, the customer (Daniel Learmont) implemented their own workaround - an EmailProcessorQueueable class that chunks email sends into batches of 100 - and confirmed this was an acceptable long-term solution, at which point the case was closed without needing the underlying product fix.
case_discussion: Detailed reproducible steps and debug logs provided upfront; Q2's product team wanted to replicate against F2F's own custom code/sandbox to investigate PDRFF-3843, but by the time they circled back the customer had already built and adopted their own chunking workaround, making further product-side investigation unnecessary for closure.
current_status: Closed - resolved via customer-built EmailProcessorQueueable workaround chunking sends into batches of 100; underlying product bulkification (PDRFF-3843) left unresolved but no longer blocking.

subject: Unable to run DAG Jobs
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: Attempting to run a DAG job for an Investor Payout Reversal (needed after a human error in a payment distributed capital back to investors incorrectly) failed with 'Too many query rows 5001' - the same governor-limit family of error seen in earlier cases (03756673, 03821271) but at a different query-row threshold.
issue_summary: Accumulated clcommon__Job_Logging__c / DAG-related logging records for the 'Default Start of Day Dynamic Jobs With Multiple Payment Mode Support' DAG exceeded the query row limit used by the DAG-running check, blocking new DAG job execution - the same recurring pattern as prior cases in this family.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) provided a SOQL query to identify and delete the excess clcommon__Job_Logging__c records (and their related Thread Logging records) tied to that DAG, clearing the row-count blockage.
case_discussion: Some initial delay coordinating a call to capture logs and replication details before Q2 provided the standard clean-up query for this recurring job-logging accumulation issue.
current_status: Closed - resolved by deleting excess DAG job-logging records per Q2's provided query.

subject: Incorrect Payout following Redemption
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: LAI-00001305 redeemed 23/06/2025, three days after its expected redemption date of 20/06/2025; the team waived interest in two steps (1 day, then 2 more days) to align the redemption statement with the originally expected Friday figures, and the amount due at closing matched the manually calculated statement exactly. However, the next day's investor payout file showed investors underpaid by a total of £2.75 relative to the expected post-waiver interest due.
issue_summary: Despite the waiver amounts being manually verified as correct and the loan-level due amount matching exactly, the actual deduction applied to Interest Posted on each IO was about £0.12/day less than the correct accrual figure for the waived days, producing a cumulative £0.35-£0.72 underpayment per IO - a subtle rounding/deduction defect in how multi-step interest waivers are applied to IO-level Interest Posted.
case_fix: Q2 (Rohit Datta) replicated the issue and escalated to engineering; determined the proper fix required incorporation into a broader new IO design, and delivered a patch (Loan Servicing 4.4001.225, Marketplace 4.4001.15 + dependent packages including CL Common 4.4000.37) in September 2025, tested through UAT/Preprod before going live around February 2026 alongside the related rounding fix from case 04189822.
case_discussion: Extended case (Jun 2025-Oct 2025) closely tied to and tested alongside case 04189822's rounding fix, given both involve IO-level Interest Posted precision; F2F (Amelia Bailey) sought clarity on patch details and uptake planning; case treated as low-recurrence so real-world confirmation deferred to future occurrences.
current_status: Closed - resolved via product patch (Loan Servicing 4.4001.225) as part of the new IO design, tested and live as of Feb 2026 alongside the related case 04189822 fix.

subject: Unable to reverse Certificate Rate Change/Reduce Interest Posted on IO
urgency: High – 2: There is major impact to your business, and key portions of the product are unusable with no reasonable way to circumvent the issue
description: After reversing a reschedule on LAI-00001415's Contract (which had moved it to a 3-months-past-maturity rate), attempting to also reverse the corresponding certificate rate change on the Investment Order threw 'Query of LOB fields caused heap usage to exceed limit' in BulkCertificateRateChangeReversalAction; a workaround attempt (backdated certificate rate change to 20 May) only rolled the due amount into accrued interest on the IO without correcting the IO's Interest Posted figure, risking a mismatch with the contract at next payment.
issue_summary: The certificate rate change reversal action hit a heap-size governor limit when processing this contract's investor loan transactions, preventing a clean reversal; the attempted workaround left IO-level Interest Posted out of sync with the contract.
case_fix: Since the contract had only one investor, Q2 (Rohit Datta) determined no rate reversal was actually needed and instead manually corrected the investor's Last Accrual Date and Accrued Interest to align with the contract's values, resolving the mismatch without needing the reversal action to succeed.
case_discussion: Customer accepted the data fix but flagged that a reliable IO-level rate-reversal mechanism is still needed for future occurrences with multiple investors, where manual correction wouldn't scale; accepted closure as a likely isolated case for now.
current_status: Closed - resolved via manual correction of investor Last Accrual Date/Accrued Interest (single-investor contract); underlying heap-limit bug in the reversal action not fixed, flagged as a risk for multi-investor recurrences.

subject: Solution for Duplicate Monthly Annual Fee (MAF) Generated on Loan Reschedule Between Billing Date and Due Date

current_status: Closed - resolved via a recommended and implemented Batch Job (size 1) approach, tested in UAT; production deployment to be scheduled by the customer.

Q2 eventually issued a further patch (4.4001.257) it says resolves the issue.
current_status: Closed – patch fix provided (Q2 Loan Servicing 4.4001.257 + dependent packages) and case closed by Q2; follow-up case 04645453 raised for post-patch sandbox issues.

subject: One Day interest difference between contract and Investor end

subject: Payout Issues on Loan 1373, 1374 & 1631 – Missing Interest Posting for Some Investment Orders
urgency: Medium – 3: There is an impact to your business, but your business continues to function
description: On loan contracts 1373, 1374 and 1631, a subset of Investment Orders had no interest posted and therefore no payout, because the last interest accrual date on those IOs had been updated to the date a fee LPT cleared (before the next posting), causing the posting job to skip them; the issue affected only some IOs, not all investors on the loan.
issue_summary: Investor Payout job silently skips interest posting (and therefore payout) for certain Investment Orders when their last accrual date was advanced by a cleared fee LPT ahead of the next scheduled posting, an intermittent/inconsistent regression affecting only a subset of IOs per loan.

current_status: Closed – patch live, no further recurrences observed (rare scenario).

subject: Backdated Payoff calculates rollback interest using current rate instead of historical rates.
urgency: Medium – 3: There is an impact to your business, but your business continues to function
description: On a backdated loan payoff (Loan Actions), the rollback interest subtracted from the payoff amount was calculated entirely at the current interest rate, ignoring a historical rate change that occurred partway through the rollback period (e.g. 3-day rollback should split 2 days at 12% and 1 day at 8%, but all 3 days were charged at 12%).
issue_summary: Reported as a bug where backdated payoff rollback interest uses only the current rate instead of blending historical rates across the rollback window; Q2 clarified this is expected behaviour because interest for the transaction date itself is not deducted, and interest is considered up to the day after the transaction date — plus a separate validation was found preventing backdated payoff before a reschedule date.
case_fix: No code fix — Q2 determined it was working as designed (system behaviour, not a defect); customer needed to reverse a rate-change reschedule before performing the backdated payoff when one existed after the target date.
case_discussion: Q2 asked whether the reschedule was via a batch job or loan actions (customer confirmed a batch job); Q2 escalated to Engineering, then explained the day-counting logic, and customer separately validated a system validation error blocking payoff dates before a reschedule date.
current_status: Closed – case approved by customer; clarified as system behaviour, no defect.

subject: Investment Orders next interest posting dates in history shows unexpected date shifts

subject: Incorrect Loan Status

description: Two loans (LAI-678, LAI-1084) moved from Active - Bad Standing to Active - Good Standing at the same timestamp (2026-02-18 00:10:27 UTC) despite still having unpaid bills; LAI-1084 later reverted to Bad Standing on 2026-05-30, but LAI-678 did not and its delinquency fields (days overdue, delinquent amount) incorrectly showed zero. F2F asked Q2 to explain the trigger and the rules governing Bad/Good Standing transitions.
issue_summary: Multiple loans intermittently flip from Active - Bad Standing to Active - Good Standing immediately upon LPT creation while payments are still uncleared, with delinquency fields not correctly reflecting the true outstanding position; root cause traced to loan__Uncleared_Repayment_Amount__c being evaluated (and, per F2F's payment process where LPTs are cleared later by a custom job, effectively miscounted) against the lock-based ACH/APC "Use Lock-Based ACH" feature during payment creation.
case_fix: Q2 concluded the behaviour was expected product behaviour for the lock-based ACH/APC enhancement (when Use Lock-Based ACH + Multiple Payment Method Support + ACH payment mode + LPT created within the APC Lock Period + uncleared amount ≥ pending bill, the loan is designed to flip to Good Standing immediately on LPT creation without waiting for clearance or the delinquency job). Workaround: removed the Lock Period from the Automated Payment Configuration so contracts don't move to Good Standing while payments remain uncleared; manual per-loan data fixes (status/delinquency field corrections) were also applied along the way.
case_discussion: Extensive investigation: Q2 initially found no log entries tied to the status change, replicated internally, escalated to Engineering, provided a list of ~15 affected contract instances, applied interim manual data fixes (e.g. LAI-678, LAI-1621), and finally explained the lock-based ACH mechanism as the root cause; F2F's custom automation was ruled out as the cause; a similar case (04645453) was cross-referenced.
current_status: Closed – identified as expected product behaviour under lock-based ACH/APC config; workaround (remove Lock Period) applied for F2F's BACS-based process.

subject: Exception: Class.loan.ApsDomainObject.processApsForPaymentCreation
urgency: Medium – 3: There is an impact to your business, but your business continues to function
description: Nightly batch logs showed a recurring exception ("Ignoring LPT creation for Contract... as Bill generation is pending", TransactionException at ApsDomainObject.processApsForPaymentCreation line 132) for LAI-1590, a loan with status 'Closed- Written Off' that F2F believed should have been excluded from the LoanPaymentTransactionCreationDynamicJob's default query, which explicitly includes 'Closed- Written Off' contracts.
issue_summary: The standard LoanPaymentTransactionCreationDynamicJob query includes contracts with status 'Closed- Written Off', causing nightly exceptions/noise for written-off loans where bill generation is pending; F2F asked whether it was safe to override the User Query to drop that status from the filter.
case_fix: Q2 confirmed it is safe to remove the 'Closed- Written Off' condition and supply a custom User Query without it, recommending it first be tested in Pre-Prod.
case_discussion: Q2 confirmed the workaround query change directly; F2F to test the modified User Query in Pre-Prod before applying to Production.
current_status: Closed – clarification/workaround (custom User Query excluding Closed- Written Off) provided; pending F2F Pre-Prod validation.

subject: Issues Post Patch Installation in Sandbox – Case ID 04412564

description: After installing the patch from case 04412564 (also linked to 04357799) in sandbox, contracts stopped transitioning to Active - Bad Standing once the delinquency grace period was exceeded; F2F replicated this three times, observing status only correcting to Bad Standing after roughly three months.
issue_summary: Same lock-based ACH/APC-driven Bad Standing → Good Standing transition behaviour reported in case 04633504, surfacing here as a post-patch regression symptom in sandbox testing (LAI-1679, 1688, 1672 used as dev test contracts).
case_fix: No separate fix — identified as a duplicate of case 04633504 (lock-based ACH/APC expected-behaviour finding); tracked and closed there instead.
case_discussion: Q2 requested the affected contract numbers, attempted internal replication (initially unsuccessful), reviewed logs (no direct entries tied to the status change), and ultimately determined this was the same root cause being investigated under case 04633504.
current_status: Closed as duplicate of case 04633504; resolution tracked there.

subject: Quick Quote Lightning Page
urgency: Medium – 3: There is an impact to your business, but your business continues to function
description: F2F overrode the default View behaviour for the managed genesis__Quick_Quotes__c object to open records on a custom Lightning Record Page with the standard Record Detail component; inline edit pencil icons do not appear on the Details tab even though standard Edit works and the user has full edit access, and the pencils are also missing on the standard Lightning view and with view?nooverride=1.
issue_summary: Inline editing is suppressed for Quick Quote (genesis__Quick_Quotes__c) records because the object's Edit action is overridden by the managed package's tabbedQuickQuote (genesis__tabbedQuickQuote) VF page, which is expected to disable standard inline-edit pencils regardless of page layout (custom or standard, Dynamic Forms or Record Detail).
case_fix: No inline-edit fix delivered — Q2/Salesforce confirmed removing/replacing the Edit override to restore standard inline editing is possible but not recommended without impact analysis (may bypass custom Quick Quote UI/save flow); as a workaround, Q2 recommended building a custom component using the Lightning Record Form component to mimic an inline-edit experience. Product team also logged Jira PDRFF-4987 to evaluate native support.
case_discussion: Extensive troubleshooting involving Q2 support, Salesforce support (separate case #473945634), and the Origination product team: confirmed the tabbedQuickQuote override as the cause, tried standard Record Detail component (same result), requested LMA/sandbox access multiple times, and ultimately provided the Lightning Record Form workaround with reference screenshots after product team declined a packaged fix pending further design details from F2F.
current_status: Closed – workaround (custom Lightning Record Form component) provided; native inline-edit support tracked separately via Jira PDRFF-4987.
